Own and manage moves, relocations, workplace changes, and associated power and data requirements across projects ranging up to and beyond $100,000.
Coordinate multiple projects and workstreams while maintaining detailed schedules, milestones and delivery plans.
Lead stakeholder meetings for large-scale moves and communicate project status, risks, decisions and next steps.

Maintain regular communication with client representatives and respond quickly to short-term operational needs.
Collect vendor proposals, communicate costs and obtain client approval before work begins.
Provide timely updates and management information throughout the project lifecycle.

Partner with the finance team to secure purchase orders for all approved vendor work.

Identify opportunities to improve resource utilization, control costs and strengthen service delivery.

Promote collaboration, accountability and service excellence across every project and workstream.

Extensive experience managing Moves, Adds & Changes, workplace relocations or related facilities projects.
Strong understanding of interior fit-out, space planning, power and data coordination, and occupancy management.
Experience overseeing subcontractors, project budgets, schedules and multiple concurrent workstreams.
Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Office, particularly Excel, Word, PowerPoint and Microsoft Project.

Strong commercial awareness, including cost control, vendor quotations, purchase orders and invoice validation.
Excellent written, verbal and presentation skills.
Demonstrated ability to build trusted relationships with diverse stakeholders.
Confidence making timely decisions throughout the project lifecycle.
Ability to remain organized, resilient and solutions-focused during periods of sustained pressure.
A consistent commitment to quality, safety and operational excellence.

Moves and workplace changes are delivered safely, on schedule and within approved budgets.
Stakeholders receive clear, timely and accurate communication.
WebCore occupancy data and project trackers remain complete and current.
Vendors consistently meet ISS standards for quality, cost, compliance and performance.
MAC KPIs and reporting requirements are achieved.
Colleagues experience smooth, well-coordinated workplace transitions.
Processes continue to evolve through collaboration, innovation and continuous improvement.

Work Environment

This position requires extended periods of computer-based work.
The role may require work outside standard business hours to oversee project activity.

Ability to lift up to 10 pounds is required.

Make Your Next Move with ISS

Bring your project leadership, workplace expertise and passion for exceptional service to ISS. In this highly visible role, you will help create seamless transitions, stronger workplace experiences and environments where people can do their best work.

Apply today and help us create places that work, think and give.

Summary

Our Newest Opportunity:

The Retirement Solutions Operations Analyst provides day-to-day operational and analytical support to the retirement operations team. This role serves as a key liaison between branch offices, operations leadership, the M&A team, technology teams, and external partners to ensure retirement plan operations are executed accurately, efficiently, and in compliance with OneDigital Investment Advisors and Broker/Dealer standards.

The Operations Analyst plays a critical role in supporting advisors, maintaining data integrity, improving operational workflows, and enabling consistent, scalable service delivery across the retirement platform. This individual serves as a trusted subject matter resource and a proactive problem-solver — someone who takes ownership of complex workflows and projects, champions data integrity, and drives continuous improvement, including through the thoughtful use of AI and automation.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities (includes but is not limited to):

Operational Support & Advisor Enablement

Serve as a primary point of contact for field offices and internal stakeholders on retirement operations-related inquiries, ensuring issues are resolved with accuracy, professionalism, and urgency.
Assist with managing the Retirement Solutions Operations (RPS OPS) shared email inbox, maintaining timely and professional responsiveness to advisors and colleagues across the organization.
Act as a subject matter resource for RPS OPS processes, applying industry knowledge and sound judgment to resolve operational issues and escalate to leadership when appropriate.
Support operational lifecycle events including cost center changes, plan terminations, and related administrative actions.
Maintain strong working relationships with Accounting and Finance partners to support training, issue resolution, and operational alignment.
Lead and manage operations projects from initiation to completion, keeping all tasks on target, on time, and aligned with team priorities.
Analyze reports indicating discrepancies in plan counts, advisors, or recordkeepers, and act to resolve identified issues.
Identify opportunities to improve operational workflows and contribute to the development of scalable processes — including the use of AI — that elevate service delivery across the retirement platform.
Support supervision and training of interns or Operations Associates on account setup and documentation review processes.

M&A Onboarding & Transition Management

Work closely with the Retirement Solutions Operations Manager to execute retirement operations responsibilities tied to new business from acquired firms or individual advisors transferring blocks of business.
Participate in weekly M&A team meetings as needed, representing retirement operations and contributing to transaction readiness and transition planning.
Serve as a knowledgeable resource on best practices, policies, and procedures throughout the transition process, ensuring a smooth and compliant handoff.
Review data and coordinate with incoming firms on current platforms and operational requirements.
Develop productive advisor and firm relationships over a compressed timeframe to facilitate efficient and effective transitions.
Manage the preparation and processing of all transition paperwork, serving as an operations contact for incoming firms on paperwork-related matters.
Liaise with Accounting to ensure all Retirement Plans are tracked through to first payment, maintaining accurate records and proactive follow-up throughout.

Conformity with all legal and regulatory requirements and guidelines associated with FINRA, SEC, and OneDigital Investment Advisors LLC compliance standards is required.
Demonstrated understanding of investment accounts, registrations, and compliance within RIA and Broker/Dealer environments.
Proficiency in Salesforce and the full Microsoft 365 Suite (Outlook, Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Teams) is required.
Experience with Fi360, Smartsheet, Orion, or other finance- or retirement-related vendor platforms is preferred.
Comfort working with data — including the ability to identify discrepancies, maintain data integrity, and produce clear operational reporting.
Comfort using AI to automate manual processes, create effective templates, and improve written communication.
Strong consultative, critical-thinking, and problem-solving skills with a bias toward action and resolution.
Exceptional organizational skills with the demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities, meet deadlines, and hold self and others accountable for deliverables.
Strong project management capabilities; able to drive complex, multi-stakeholder initiatives from planning through execution.
Outstanding written and verbal communication skills; able to present clearly and succinctly across diverse audiences and adapt communication style accordingly.
High degree of composure and adaptability — able to manage increasing workloads in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment with professionalism and calm.
Customer-focused mindset with interpersonal agility to work effectively across different personality types and organizational levels.
Superior follow-through and follow-up discipline; thrives in a high-energy, collaborative team environment.
Previous experience in a customer or client support role is preferred.

Education, Training And Experience

An undergraduate degree in Business, Information Technology, Accounting, Finance, Economics, or a related field is required; equivalent work experience will be considered.
4–5 years of business experience required, preferably in management of technology, processes, and people within the investment or financial services industry.
Required: Proficiency in Salesforce and the Microsoft 365 Suite.
Preferred: Experience with Fi360, Smartsheet, Orion, or other finance- or retirement-related vendor platforms.

jobs.title: Sales Enablement Program Manager
jobs.description:
Description

Join Team CARFAX as a Sales Enablement Program Manager

Isn't it time you bragged about where you work? At CARFAX, we do, every day. We pride ourselves on being mission-focused on helping to grow a brand built on accuracy and integrity. We care deeply about our products and our customers. We’re more than just a company: We help millions of consumers make more-informed decisions every day. We know that our teammates are our most valuable asset, and we value a balanced life while tackling challenging projects in a fast-paced environment.

About The Role

CARFAX is investing in its Revenue Enablement function, and the Sales Enablement Program Manager is central to that effort. This is a hands-on, high-impact role focused on sharpening the skills, process discipline, and execution of our DBU sales teams — Field Sales, Hybrid Field Sales, Strategic Sales, and Inside Sales.

You’ll spend the majority of your time embedded in the flow of the sales org: coaching reps and frontline managers, reinforcing our sales process and methodology, and building the programs, content, and tools that help sellers win. You’ll also serve as a strategic partner to sales leadership — bringing field insight and enablement expertise into decisions about process, change, and go-to-market execution. This is a builder’s role on a growing team, so you’ll help shape how enablement operates at CARFAX while delivering results from day one.

What You’ll Be Doing

Enable all DBU sales roles. Serve as the dedicated enablement partner to Field Sales, Strategic Sales, and Inside Sales — tailoring programs, coaching, and content to the distinct motions, customer profiles, and performance goals of each team. One size doesn’t fit all; what works for a field rep calling on independent dealers is different from what an inside seller needs to convert on the phone.
Build and lead training and coaching. Own the design, delivery, and continuous improvement of sales training on core selling fundamentals — discovery, value articulation, objection handling, negotiation, and pipeline management. Provide hands-on coaching to reps and managers through field ride-alongs, call reviews, and deal reviews. Equip frontline managers to reinforce these skills with their own teams so your impact scales across the org. Best-in-class enablement functions treat training as a continuous discipline, not a one-time event — this mindset is the foundation of the role.
Reinforce process, methodology, and tools. Drive consistent adoption of CARFAX’s sales process and methodology through sustained, ongoing reinforcement. Champion adoption of the supporting tech stack — CRM, conversation intelligence, enablement platforms — so reps work smarter and sales leaders have the visibility they need to coach effectively.
Build assets and codify best practices. Create and maintain polished, field-ready sales assets — playbooks, battle cards, talk tracks, pitch decks, and process guides. Surface what top performers do differently through field observation, call reviews, and win/loss patterns, and systematically distribute those insights across the sales org. Ensuring reps have access to the right content at the right moment in the sales cycle is a core enablement discipline.
Partner on the onboarding handoff. Work closely with the Onboarding Lead to ensure a seamless transition from new hire onboarding into ongoing, role-based enablement. This role does not own onboarding, but its success depends on a tight partnership with the person who does.
Serve as a strategic partner to sales leadership. Act as a trusted advisor to DBU sales leadership on how to raise seller performance and execution quality. Bring the field’s perspective into internal decisions on process roll-outs, change management, and product launches — ensuring the field is ready to execute before go-to-market, not after.
Collaborate cross-functionally. Partner with Revenue Operations to define and track the KPIs that demonstrate enablement’s impact on pipeline health, conversion rates, and revenue performance. Partner with Marketing on sales assets, messaging, and go-to-market motions — so programs are data-informed and what reps carry into the field is aligned, current, and on-brand.

Required

What we’re looking for:

3+ years of sales enablement experience, ideally supporting multiple, distinct sales motions simultaneously.
Experience carrying a sales quota — you’ve sold, and you understand the seller’s world firsthand.
A demonstrated track record of designing and delivering training and coaching programs that measurably change rep behavior and drive revenue outcomes.
Strong facilitation, communication, and coaching skills — both in-person and virtually — including the ability to create compelling, polished presentations in PowerPoint (or equivalent tools).
The ability to build trust and influence without authority across reps, managers, senior leadership, and cross-functional partners.
Comfort operating in a build-from-scratch environment where structure, programs, and processes don’t fully exist yet — and you’ll help create them.
Experience with a formal sales methodology (e.g., MEDDIC/MEDDPICC, Integrity Selling, Challenger, SPIN, or similar) and a track record of reinforcing it in the field over time.
Ability to travel up to 10% of the time to coach reps in the field and support team events.

Preferred

Automotive industry or automotive technology experience — familiarity with how dealerships operate, how they buy, and what they value is a meaningful advantage in this role.
Experience supporting a blend of field, strategic/enterprise, and inside sales teams within a single organization.
Hands-on experience with conversation intelligence tools (e.g., Gong, Chorus), Salesforce, learning management systems (LMS), and content management systems (CMS).

What’s In It For You

Competitive compensation, benefits and generous time-off policies
4-Day summer work weeks and a winter holiday break
401(k) / DCPP matching
Annual bonus program
Casual, dog-friendly, and innovative office spaces.

Don’t Just Take Our Word For It

13x VA Best Places to Work
12x Top Workplaces in Washington (Presented by The Washington Post and WTOP)
9x Washingtonian Great Place to Work
5x USA Today Top Workplaces
5x St. Louis Post-Dispatch Best Places to Work

The anticipated annual base salary range for this position is $110,000 - $150,000. Actual compensation within this range will be determined based on a variety of factors, including geographic location, relevant experience, skills, qualifications, and internal equity considerations.

Carfax is committed to providing competitive compensation that reflects local market conditions and individual contributions. In addition to base salary, employees may be eligible for incentive compensation, long-term incentives, and a comprehensive benefits package, where applicable.

About CARFAX And S&P Global Mobility

S&P Global has recently announced the intent to separate our Mobility Segment into a standalone public company.

CARFAX, part of S&P Global Mobility, helps millions of people every day confidently shop, buy, service and sell used cars with innovative solutions powered by CARFAX vehicle history information. The expert in vehicle history since 1984, CARFAX provides exclusive services like CARFAX Used Car Listings, CARFAX Car Care, CARFAX History-Based Value and the flagship CARFAX® Vehicle History Report™ to consumers and the automotive industry. new_jobs.title: People Project Manager
new_jobs.description:
Who are we?

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company. We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!

Why This Role?

We're hiring a People Project Manager
to join our HR PMO
and help deliver an ambitious portfolio of HR programs, products, and initiatives as we scale globally.

This is not a business-as-usual project management role
. We're a hypergrowth company building at speed, and our HR team is building alongside it. We're looking for someone who gets genuine energy from bringing order to chaos, creating structure where there isn't any yet, and getting important things shipped.

Hypergrowth, for real. Things move fast, priorities evolve, and there's always something meaningful to jump into. If you love pace, variety, and figuring things out as you go, you'll have a huge canvas here.
A chance to build. Our HR PMO is taking shape within a hugely ambitious HR team. You'll help create the workflows, rhythms, and tools we need to build a world-class function at scale.
Real ownership. Take projects from idea to delivery — creating structure, driving actions, managing dependencies, and keeping teams moving.
Global from day one. Work across our distributed HR team and with stakeholders around the world.

You'll Thrive If You

Create order from chaos: Turn fast-moving, ambiguous problems into clear plans and outcomes
Are relentlessly organized: Stay ahead of details, dependencies, decisions, and follow-ups
Love pace: Move quickly, adapt as things change, and keep momentum high
Build great workflows: Find simpler, smarter, more scalable ways to get things done
Collaborate brilliantly: Bring stakeholders together and create clarity across teams
Think and do: Build the plan, then roll up your sleeves to get it over the line

You'll Help Drive

HR projects: Manage programs and initiatives across our global HR roadmap
Planning & delivery: Build plans, milestones, workstreams, and clear ownership
Cross-functional execution: Coordinate across HR, Finance, Legal, IT, and other teams
Project governance: Drive decisions, manage risks and dependencies, and keep stakeholders aligned
Better ways of working: Build repeatable workflows and tools that help HR execute at scale

We're Looking For Someone Who

3+ years of experience: Project or program management in a fast-moving, high-growth organization
Is an excellent project manager: Can independently drive complex, multi-stakeholder projects from start to finish
Is hyper-organized: Exceptional attention to detail and strong systems for managing work
Builds, not just operates: Gets excited by creating something new rather than maintaining business as usual
Manages stakeholders well: Creates alignment and accountability without relying on authority
Communicates exceptionally: Produces crisp plans, updates, and documentation
Is pro-team: Collaborative, low-ego, and invested in making the whole team better

Location

This is a global, remote role
, working across our distributed HR organization and with stakeholders around the world.

Full-Time Employees At Cohere Enjoy These Perks

A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch.
Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health.
RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme.
100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent.
Annual enrichment benefits:

Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit.

Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching.

6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!)
Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite.

How And Where We Work

Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon.
For those in the office: a daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community and social events.
For those not near an office: a co-working benefit so you can work alongside others in your city.
Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly.

If any of the above doesn’t line up exactly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply.

We strive to create an inclusive work environment for all; we welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to providing equal opportunities. Should you require any accommodations during the recruitment process, please submit an Accommodations Request Form, and we will work together to meet your needs.

We may use AI-enabled tools to screen and assess applicants against the criteria for this position. This helps our recruiters identify potentially qualified candidates, but it doesn't limit the applications our recruiters may review or consider.

Beware of Scams: Cohere will never ask for payment or third-party services (e.g., CV writing) as part of our hiring process. All legitimate roles are listed on the Cohere careers page and LinkedIn only, with all communications from Cohere employees coming from an @cohere.com or @cw.cohere email alias. If jobs are viewed on other sites then please verify these through our official careers page.

new_jobs.title: Senior Project Manager, Contact Center
new_jobs.description:
Presidio, Where Teamwork and Innovation Shape the Future

At Presidio, we're at the forefront of a global technology revolution, transforming industries through cutting-edge digital solutions and next-generation AI. We empower businesses - and their internal customers - to achieve more through innovation, automation, and intelligent insights.

The Role

Presidio is seeking an experienced, customer-facing Senior Project Manager to lead the delivery of complex Contact Center and Unified Communications solutions within a Value-Added Reseller (VAR) and IT Systems Integrator environment. This role is accountable for the end-to-end execution of large-scale on-premises, hybrid, and cloud contact center implementations, often involving multiple technologies, vendors, and stakeholders across extended delivery timelines.

The Senior Project Manager owns project outcomes from contract handoff through production rollout and closeout, ensuring strict adherence to Statement of Work (SOW) scope, schedule, budget, margin targets, and customer satisfaction objectives.

Responsibilities Include

Key Responsibilities

Project Delivery & Governance

Provide end-to-end ownership of all project phases including requirements validation, detailed planning, solution design coordination, build, testing, deployment, stabilization, and formal project closeout.
Develop, maintain, and actively manage integrated project plans, including work breakdown structures, critical path analysis, milestones, dependencies, and deliverables.
Enforce project governance standards to ensure projects are delivered on time, within approved budget, and in alignment with contractual commitments.

Financial & Commercial Management

Own project financial performance, including revenue recognition alignment, cost tracking, billable utilization, and gross margin targets.
Monitor and control project labor, materials, and third-party costs; provide accurate forecasting, variance analysis, and financial reporting.
Partner with accounting and operations teams to ensure accurate project billing, cost allocation, and compliance with internal financial controls.

Resource & Stakeholder Management

Lead cross-functional project teams consisting of Presidio engineering resources, solution architects, third-party vendors, and subcontractors.
Perform proactive resource planning in coordination with delivery leadership to ensure appropriate staffing, skills alignment, and capacity availability.
Act as the primary point of contact for customers, executive sponsors, internal leadership, and vendor partners throughout the project lifecycle.

Change, Risk & Quality Management

Identify, document, and manage project risks, issues, and mitigation strategies; escalate appropriately with clear impact analysis and recommended actions.
Lead formal change management processes, including scope change assessment, pricing impacts, schedule adjustments, and customer approvals.
Ensure all deliverables meet Presidio quality standards, contractual requirements, and customer expectations prior to acceptance.

Customer Engagement & Relationship Management

Drive clear, consistent, and professional communication through status reports, steering meetings, and executive briefings.
Proactively address client concerns, manage expectations, and resolve delivery challenges to maintain trust and long-term customer relationships.
Represent Presidio as a trusted advisor, reinforcing a consultative delivery approach that supports repeat business and account growth.

Technology Domain Awareness

Maintain working knowledge and experience with enterprise contact center and collaboration platforms to effectively manage solution delivery, risks, and dependencies, including:
Cisco Contact Center Express (UCCX) and Contact Center Enterprise (UCCE)
Cisco Unified Communications
Cisco Customer Voice Portal (CVP)
Webex Contact Center and Webex Contact Center Enterprise
AWS
Genesys
Five9
Twilio Flex
CCAI

Required Skills And Professional Experience

Bachelor’s degree or equivalent professional or military experience.
7+ years of hands-on experience as a Senior Project Manager delivering complex, customer-facing technology implementation projects within a VAR, systems integrator, or professional services environment.
Demonstrated experience managing Contact Center and Unified Communications solutions, including cloud, hybrid, and on-prem deployments.
Proven ability to manage project financials, including margin, utilization, cost controls, and revenue alignment.
Strong command of formal project management methodologies, documentation, and governance practices.
Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Project for scheduling, dependency management, and critical path analysis.
PMP, Agile, or equivalent project management certification preferred.

Your future at Presidio

Joining Presidio means stepping into a culture of trailblazers - thinkers, builders, and collaborators - who push the boundaries of what's possible. With our expertise AI-driven analytics, cloud solutions, cybersecurity, and next-gen infrastructure, we enable businesses to stay ahead in an ever-evolving digital world.

Here, your impact is real. Whether you're harnessing the power of Generative AI, architecting resilient digital ecosystems, or driving data-driven transformation, you'll be part of a team that is shaping the future.

Ready to innovate? Let's redefine what's next-together.

About Presidio

Presidio is committed to hiring the most qualified candidates to join our amazing culture. We aim to attract and hire top talent from all backgrounds, including underrepresented and marginalized communities. We encourage women, people of color, people with disabilities, and veterans to apply for open roles at Presidio. Diversity of skills and thought is a key component to our business success.

At Presidio, speed and quality meet technology and innovation. Presidio is a trusted ally for organizations across industries with a decades-long history of building traditional IT foundations and deep expertise in AI and automation, security, networking, digital transformation, and cloud computing. Presidio fills gaps, removes hurdles, optimizes costs, and reduces risk. Presidio's expert technical team develops custom applications, provides managed services, and enables actionable data insights and builds forward-thinking solutions that drive strategic outcomes for clients globally. new_jobs.title: Project Manager - Advisory
new_jobs.description:
At Signant Health, we help bring life-changing treatments to patients faster. We are a global evidence generation company that supports clinical trials with smart technology, scientific expertise, and hands-on operational support — so better data leads to better decisions in healthcare. We embrace AI and advanced technologies to enhance every aspect of what we do, from data analysis to operational efficiency.

Our teams work at the intersection of science, technology, and patient experience, delivering digital solutions powered by AI innovation that make clinical trials more efficient, more accurate, and more accessible around the world. Trusted by leading pharmaceutical companies and CROs, our platforms and services support studies across more than 90 countries and have contributed to hundreds of new drug approvals.

If you are motivated by meaningful work, global impact, and innovation in clinical research and digital health — including the opportunity to work with cutting-edge AI technologies — you will find purpose and opportunity at Signant Health.

About The Role

The Project Manager is responsible for the planning, execution, and completion of projects considering budget, timelines, resources, and task management. You will communicate transparently and in a timely manner with assigned Signant Health clients and internal stakeholders, managing project risks and ensuring timely resolution while reporting status with appropriate internal and external stakeholders. This role requires an effective leader who excels in problem-solving, can motivate a result-oriented team, and builds trust-based relationships with Signant Health clients. You will contribute to the implementation of company-wide process improvements to ensure effective and efficient project delivery.

KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES - Function

Manage and lead initial project delivery tasks, including the software development lifecycle (SDLC) of simple to medium complexity studies.
Ensure project systems are built and released in accordance with client expectations; lead the project system change control process.
Support implementation of complex, multi-product projects as needed.
Manage projects in accordance with established timelines, budgets, quality standards, and contractual requirements.
Review, approve, and maintain project and corporate systems and documentation.
Handle client escalations independently; work with internal and client teams to resolve issues and escalate as appropriate in a timely manner.
Serve as the primary contact for customers on assigned projects; ensure quality of communication with clients in terms of cadence, content, and audience.
Manage financial health of assigned projects, including vendor services, licensing, payments, invoicing, devices, resource assignments, and vendor management activities.
Collaborate with other functional areas to ensure project delivery meets timelines and client expectations within budget.
Identify and document Incident Reports with Quality Management; coordinate client notification and closure.
Report project status updates to internal and external stakeholders.

DECISION MAKING AND INFLUENCE

Demonstrated ability to lead through influence.
Capable of weighing risks and making decisions that align with Signant values and strategy.
Manage customer escalations effectively, with follow-up and closure.

Knowledge, Skills & Attributes

Essential:

Bachelor's degree or equivalent professional experience
Proven experience in a Project Management role or equivalent
Understanding of the software development life cycle and specification and configuration of software products
Demonstrated ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously with excellent time management, communication (oral and written), and organizational skills
Detail-oriented with focus on first-time quality delivery
Proficiency with MS Office Suite (Word, Excel, MS Project, PowerPoint)
Ability to communicate effectively with all levels of the organization; comfortable presenting to diverse and large audiences
Proven ability to direct project activities, ensure customer satisfaction, and adhere to study budgets
Must show initiative and be able to work independently as needed

Desirable:

Background in pharmaceutical, medical device, medical education, or CRO industries
Experience with clinical trials, pharmaceutical industry, or life sciences
Knowledge of the clinical research environment and Good Clinical Practice (GCP) principles
Project Management Professional (PMP) or equivalent certification

new_jobs.title: Senior Strategic Implementation Manager
new_jobs.description:
Kestra Financial is a wealth management platform dedicated to empowering independent financial professionals—including traditional and hybrid RIAs—to grow their businesses and deliver exceptional client service. We combine advanced business management technology with personalized consulting to provide unmatched scale, efficiency, and support. Our advisor-focused culture is built on innovation and advocacy, enabling advisors to offer comprehensive securities and investment advisory solutions to their clients

Lead with Purpose. Partner with Impact

Kestra Financial, a leading provider of wealth management platforms, technology solutions, and investment products empowering independent financial advisors and RIAs nationwide, is seeking a Senior Strategic Implementation Manager.

This role serves as a pivotal execution leader accountable for the disciplined delivery of Kestra Wealth Management’s highest-priority strategic initiatives in investment products and platform capabilities. You will drive the successful launch of new investment products and manage end-to-end launch campaigns while coordinating complex cross-functional projects spanning technology, compliance, business development, and operations.

By implementing and championing agile, Scrum-like cadences and robust portfolio governance practices, you will build transparency, predictability, and accountability across initiatives. Your leadership will ensure that strategic intent translates into measurable business outcomes—including accelerated advisor adoption, revenue contribution from new products, enhanced platform capabilities, and operational excellence.

This is a hands-on, high-impact role for a collaborative leader who thrives at the intersection of strategy, execution, and cross-functional influence in a dynamic, growth-oriented wealth management environment.

What You’ll Do:

Own the end-to-end governance and planning that results in successful delivery of priority investment product launches (e.g., alternative investment solutions, insurance products, or curated offerings) and strategic platform implementation initiatives (new advisory revenue vertical, investment program redesign, etc) from concept through post-launch optimization and benefits realization.
Lead the coordination and execution of comprehensive launch campaigns, aligning go-to-market activities including sales enablement, marketing communications, advisor training and onboarding programs, distribution strategy, and adoption tracking to drive rapid uptake and sustained engagement.
Establish and maintain a prioritized portfolio of strategic initiatives for Investment Platforms & Products; drive rigorous sequencing, capacity alignment, funding discipline, and proactive trade-off decisions (scope, timeline, resources, investment) aligned to Kestra’s business objectives and growth priorities.
Partner with Product Management to translate product strategy and roadmap into executable implementation plans with clear milestones, dependencies, and success criteria.
Support Wealth Management platform and product leads by facilitating high-performing cross-functional project teams and workstreams involving:
Technology: Platform development, data integrations (including MDM/medallion architectures), APIs, advisor portals/tools, and infrastructure enhancements.
Compliance & Legal: Product due diligence, regulatory reviews/approvals, disclosures, risk assessments, and ongoing product governance to ensure adherence to SEC, FINRA, fiduciary, and other requirements.
Business: Commercialization strategy, RIA/advisor engagement and feedback loops, distribution channel readiness, pricing/packaging, and P&L impact modeling.
Operations & Finance: Operational readiness, process design, financial tracking, and benefits measurement.
Map and manage complex dependencies, risks, and interdependencies across teams; proactively identify and remove blockers while fostering alignment and shared ownership in a matrixed environment.
Ensure every initiative incorporates appropriate compliance guardrails, risk controls, audit readiness, and change management from the start.
Design, implement, and continuously mature agile delivery operating models tailored to regulated investment product and platform initiatives. This includes establishing Scrum-like cadences (sprint planning, daily stand-ups, sprint reviews, retrospectives), Kanban for workflow transparency and flow optimization, and scaled frameworks (e.g., program-level planning or release management) for larger or interdependent efforts.
Stand up consistent governance rhythms and forums, including steering committees, launch readiness reviews/tollgates, dependency management sessions, risk reviews, and clear escalation paths to executive leadership.
Drive adoption of modern agile/project tools (Jira, Confluence, Azure DevOps, or equivalent) and best practices to improve delivery velocity, predictability, collaboration, and quality across technology and business teams.
Champion a shift toward iterative, outcome-focused delivery—balancing the need for structure and compliance in product launches with the speed and adaptability required in a competitive wealth tech landscape.
Build and operate a portfolio “control tower” capability: deliver timely, credible, decision-oriented reporting and dashboards on initiative status, milestones, risks/issues, dependencies, financial performance (budget vs. plan, ROI tracking), and leading indicators of business impact.
Define, track, and report on key business outcome metrics tied to each strategic initiative (e.g., new product net flows/AUM/revenue contribution, advisor adoption and usage rates, client/advisor satisfaction or NPS impact, reduction in time-to-market or launch cycle time, compliance adherence, platform feature utilization and engagement).
Proactively surface execution risks, capacity constraints, and recommended trade-offs to senior leadership; lead structured issue resolution, corrective action planning, and recovery efforts to protect delivery commitments and protect/enhance business results.
Prepare and present high-quality materials for executive leadership, steering committees, and governance forums; represent the delivery health and outlook of the Investment Platforms & Products portfolio with clarity and fact-based insights.
Instill a culture of genuine accountability—where teams own and are measured on the delivery of agreed business outcomes and value realization, not merely activity completion or milestone hitting.

What You Bring: 

Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Economics, Business, or Software Engineering.
2+ years experience in technical product management in an Agile environment.
5+ years of experience in wealth management, investment operations, or trading
3-5+ years of progressive leadership experience in strategic program/portfolio management, product implementation, launch execution, or enterprise transformation roles within wealth management, RIA platforms, investment product development, fintech, asset/wealth platforms, or similarly complex, regulated financial services environments.
Demonstrated success leading multiple end-to-end launches of investment products or major platform capabilities, including coordination across technology builds, compliance/regulatory approvals, and go-to-market execution
Direct experience with alternatives/private markets access, model portfolios, structured solutions, or advisor-facing technology platforms within a broker dealer organization is strongly preferred.
Track record of successfully implementing or significantly maturing agile delivery practices (Scrum, Kanban, SAFe, hybrid, or tailored approaches) in product development or regulated contexts, with quantifiable improvements in predictability, velocity, and time-to-value.

Certifications and Licenses:

Series 7 , 63 or 66 required within 2 years.
Series 65 preferred

Internal Application Policy:

Internal applicants must be in good standing and have a minimum of 1 year of service with Kestra. Internal applicants must also have a minimum of 1 year service in current role unless approved by EVP.

Benefits to support you:

Competitive pay and benefits with a large employer (over 1600 employees nationwide)
401(k), health insurance, and a competitive benefits package
Work in a supportive, collaborative environment committed to professional excellence
Help clients navigate meaningful financial decisions with confidence
Opportunities for training, development, and long-term growth within the firm
Tuition reimbursement for qualified expenses

Kestra Values:

Our Mission is Powering Financial Independence, enabling the growth and success of investing clients and the advisors who serve them. We do that by living our values: Serve, Make it Happen, and One team.

new_jobs.title: Program Manager, Marauder
new_jobs.description:
Saronic Technologies is a leader in revolutionizing autonomy at sea, dedicated to developing state-of-the-art solutions that enhance maritime operations through autonomous and intelligent platforms.

Job Overview

Saronic Technologies is seeking a Program Manager to own the execution and delivery of Marauder, our 180-foot Autonomous Surface Vessel (ASV) produced at our Franklin, LA shipyard. This is a flagship large-scale production program, and the Program Manager is accountable for its cost, schedule, scope, and customer outcomes from contract award through delivery and sustainment.

Marauder is built at production scale and fielded across a wide and evolving range of complex missions. The Program Manager must pair deep expertise in large-scale shipbuilding and rate production with an instinct for modular kits, payloads, and mission-package integration—understanding how a common hull is configured, re-configured, and sustained to meet diverse customer needs. This role owns the balance between production throughput and mission flexibility.

The Program Manager serves as the primary customer-facing owner of the program, partnering closely with the internal Saronic growth, engineering, production and quality teams. The right candidate brings the customer fluency to manage government stakeholders and contracts, the technical acumen to make technical decisions aligned to the customer needs and contract requirements, and the programmatic discipline to deliver a large, complex platform at scale.

Responsibilities

Program Ownership & Delivery

Own end-to-end execution of the Marauder program, holding accountability for cost, schedule, scope, and quality from award through delivery and sustainment.
Serve as a leader and owner of the customer contract, deliverables, milestones, CDRLs, and contractual obligations.
Build and maintain the integrated program plan, aligning productions scheduled, engineering milestones, and integration timelines to customer commitments.
Drive risk and opportunity management across the program, escalating and resolving issues that threaten cost, schedule, or performance.
Report program health, forecasts, and decisions to Saronic leadership and customer stakeholders.

Large-Scale Production Interface

Partner with the Franklin production team to plan and execute rate production of a 180-foot ASV, from long-lead procurement through hull construction, outfitting, and delivery.
Monitor build sequencing, work breakdown, and production milestones to protect throughput while meeting quality and acceptance criteria.
Monitor and mitigate production risks—supply chain, labor, tooling, and facility constraints—unique to large-vessel shipbuilding.
Coordinate with Quality and Production to ensure build configurations and acceptance events meet customer and contractual standards.

Kit & Mission Package Integration

Own the configuration strategy for Marauder across a variety of mission packages, kits, and payloads on a common production hull.
Partner with Mission Package Integration Managers to plan integration of bespoke and commercial-off-the-shelf kits into the production and delivery flow.
Balance production standardization against mission-driven variance, protecting throughput while enabling flexibility.
Ensure integration timelines, dependencies, and configuration baselines are reflected in the master program plan.
Capture mission-package lessons learned and feed them back into production and product roadmaps.

Customer & Stakeholder Engagement

Serve as the primary point of contact for the customer, managing expectations, requirements, and relationships across the program lifecycle.
Elicit and clarify evolving mission needs, translating them into actionable program and technical direction.
Lead program reviews, delivery events, and technical exchanges with government stakeholders, operators, and evaluators.
Deliver clear, concise program updates and after-action reporting to leadership and customer audiences.

Cross-Functional Leadership

Direct and synchronize a cross-functional program team spanning Production, Engineering, Software, Mission Services, and Forward Deployed Engineering.
Partner with Technical Program Managers to align technical execution with programmatic commitments.
Make and defend tradeoff decisions across capability, schedule, cost, and risk.
Drive disciplined configuration management across vessels, kits, payloads, and software versions

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Naval Architecture, or a related technical field.
10+ years of experience in program management of large-scale production, shipbuilding, or complex defense development programs. Program Management experience of Unmanned Surface Vessels highly desirable.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to interface confidently with technical and non-technical audiences.
Demonstrated ownership of cost, schedule, and scope on programs of significant size and complexity.
Experience managing production at rate, including supply chain, build sequencing, and delivery of large or complex hardware systems highly desirable.
Proven ability to manage government or defense customers, contracts, and deliverables.
Willingness to travel up to 25% of the time.
Secret security clearance eligibility required, active preferred.

Key Competencies

Can own a large, complex program end-to-end while balancing production throughput against mission flexibility.
Can connect production and configuration decisions to overall program cost, schedule, and mission outcomes.
Can translate evolving customer requirements into disciplined, executable program plans.
Leadership of high-performing, cross-functional, and distributed teams.
Established track record of clear, consistent, and correct communications with peers, leaders, and external stakeholders.
Comfort guiding customers through ambiguous or evolving requirements and shaping actionable solutions.

Physical Demands

Prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer
Occasional standing and walking within the office
Manual dexterity to operate a computer keyboard, mouse, and other office equipment
Visual acuity to read screens, documents, and reports
Occasional reaching, bending, or stooping to access file drawers, cabinets, or office supplies
Lifting and carrying items up to 20 pounds occasionally (e.g., office supplies, packages)

new_jobs.description:
Job Description

Primary program POC with management responsibility and overall cost/schedule/technical accountability for a single major/critical subcontract, or portfolio of large program subcontracts performance, risk management and tracking. Plan, organize, direct, and control significant program subcontract management activities in support of an SMS proposal or program. Ensure supplier execution of all subcontract requirements for cost, schedule, technical, and mission assurance. Additionally, maintain positive internal and external relations with the BAE Systems Space & Mission Systems (SMS) customer, the program team, and the supplier(s).

The Operations Strategic Capabilities Unit plays a fundamental role in enabling efficient business and program execution – from strategic capital investments, industrial operations and an efficient supply chain, to state-of-the-art manufacturing and test operations and top-notch facilities management.

The Integrated Supply Chain team has a direct impact on program success, acting as a critical chain that links the end-to-end material flow together. Our organization helps propel us forward and achieve true mission partnership.

What You’ll Do

Responsible for overall leadership and management of a single program subcontract or a portfolio of program subcontracts, with clear lines of authority defined at the program level. Primary Program POC to all Program subcontract stakeholders with responsibility for subcontract cost, schedule, technical, quality, and all deliverables going to/from subcontractor(s).
Participate in proposal preparation activities in support of new business capture opportunities with existing and/or new subcontractors, customers, and programs. Coordinate compilation of supplier RFP packages to align to customer proposal scope, timelines, and objectives. Coordinate SME inputs to technical evaluations of complex subcontractor proposals, assessing realism, reasonableness, and completeness.
May lead development of Program Subcontract Management Plan (PSMP).
Lead the program Subcontract Management Team (SMT) and aligns with the program to ensure the SMT is staffed with appropriate skill levels and that internal work is being accomplished according to plan in support of the subcontract management plan.
Ensure program mission requirements, purposes, objectives, and expectations are communicated and flowed to the subcontractor(s). Responsible for development and execution of subcontract: management plan, scope of work, technical requirements, mission assurance requirements, milestones, SDRLs and any other subcontract(s) deliverables necessary.
Responsible for all subcontract(s) deliverables to the various program levels, as applicable.
Program level budgetary authority for subcontract execution including profit/loss, labor budget, management reserve, and all aspects of oversight and management of the subcontract(s).
Responsible for subcontract cost tracking, Earned Value (EV) and EAC budget, variance tracking and reporting requirements, including management, and monitoring timely supplier financial reporting.
Ensure visibility and communication of subcontract technical, quality assurance, financial, schedule, and compliance to Program reporting requirements.
Responsible for subcontract schedule and program level schedule margin specific to the subcontract(s). Ensure supplier IMS is integrated into the Program level IMS.
Manage the subcontract(s) risks including subcontract(s) cost, schedule, technical and quality risks. Responsible for deconflicting resource and schedule conflicts at subcontractor(s) location. Responsibility and know-how to leverage program and SMS team in achieving efficient conflict resolution.
Responsible for subcontract(s) change control and management. Support change proposal efforts for subcontract(s) including pre-coordination with subcontractor(s) to establish expectations. Lead internal evaluation of subcontractor(s) change proposals and development of negotiation plans
In partnership with the Subcontract Manager (SMS’ empowered official for the subcontract), act as the principal interface with the subcontractor on all subcontract related subjects and perform as a liaison between subcontractor, Program, and other stakeholders as needed.
Work closely with and assist Subcontract Manager to ensure Subcontract is maintained current and meets Program requirements. Establish SMS programmatic negotiation position and support subcontract negotiations.
Work closely with Program Management and customer to communicate subcontractor progress, resolve issues and concerns, and identify and manage subcontractor risk.
Coordinate the participants, schedule, logistics, and success criteria and chair subcontractor program status, business, design, manufacturing, test and pre-ship reviews, including inclusion of Customer participation.
May develop and manage a complete Subcontractor Performance system to tie past performance, current requirements, and subcontract documentation and management into predictive subcontractor performance model.
Ensure that all business is conducted using the highest ethical standards and in compliance with all applicable laws, statutes, and regulations.
Maintain a regular and predictable work schedule.
Establish and maintain effective working relationships within the department, the Strategic Business Units, Strategic Capabilities Units and the Company. Interact appropriately with others in order to maintain a positive and productive work environment.
Perform other duties as necessary.

On-Site Work Environment:

This position requires regular in-person engagement by working

on-site five days

each normally scheduled week in the primary work location. Travel and local commute between company campuses and other possible non-company locations may be required.

Working Conditions

Work is performed in an office environment, laboratory, cleanroom, or production floor.

Short Term Incentive:

Subject to business performance and recommendations of management, this role may be eligible to participate in an incentive compensation plan.

Required Education, Experience, & Skills

BS/BA in related field plus 10 or more years related experience.
Each higher-level degree, i.e., Master’s Degree or Ph.D., may substitute for two years of experience. Related technical experience may be considered in lieu of education. Degree must be from a university, college, or school which is accredited by an agency recognized by the US Secretary of Education, US Department of Education.
A current, active Top Secret/SCI security clearance is required with the ability to obtain and maintain a Top Secret/SCI Polygraph.

Pay Information

Full-Time Salary Range: $134640 - $228888

Please note: This range is based on our market pay structures. However, individual salaries are determined by a variety of factors including, but not limited to: business considerations, local market conditions, and internal equity, as well as candidate qualifications, such as skills, education, and experience.

Employee Benefits: At BAE Systems, we support our employees in all aspects of their life, including their health and financial well-being. Regular employees scheduled to work 20+ hours per week are offered: health, dental, and vision insurance; health savings accounts; a 401(k) savings plan; disability coverage; and life and accident insurance. We also have an employee assistance program, a legal plan, and other perks including discounts on things like home, auto, and pet insurance. Our leave programs include paid time off, paid holidays, as well as other types of leave, including paid parental, military, bereavement, and any applicable federal and state sick leave. Employees may participate in the company recognition program to receive monetary or non-monetary recognition awards. Other incentives may be available based on position level and/or job specifics.

About BAE Systems Space & Mission Systems

BAE Systems, Inc. is the U.S. subsidiary of BAE Systems plc, an international defense, aerospace and security company which delivers a full range of products and services for air, land and naval forces, as well as advanced electronics, security, information technology solutions and customer support services. Improving the future and protecting lives is an ambitious mission, but it’s what we do at BAE Systems. Working here means using your passion and ingenuity where it counts – defending national security with breakthrough technology, superior products, and intelligence solutions. As you develop the latest technology and defend national security, you will continually hone your skills on a team—making a big impact on a global scale. At BAE Systems, you’ll find a rewarding career that truly makes a difference.

Headquartered in Boulder, Colorado, Space & Mission Systems is a leading provider of national defense and civil space applications, advanced remote sensing, scientific and tactical systems for government and commercial customers. We continually pioneer ways to innovate spacecraft, mission payloads, optical systems, and other defense and civil capabilities. Powered by endlessly curious people with an unwavering mission focus, we continually discover ways to enable our customers to perform beyond expectation and protect what matters most.

Job Overview

Saronic Technologies is seeking a Program Manager of Mission Package Integration to lead the development, integration, and delivery of modules, kits, and mission packages onto Saronic’s growing portfolio of Autonomous Surface Vessel (ASV) programs.

The Mission Package Integrations PM is a technical executor focusing on bridging Saronic platforms with both bespoke and commercial off the shelf kits, modules, and payloads. This role focuses on supporting existing customer contracts, strategizing new product lines, and driving organic growth through Saronic and customer-derived mission packages.

Technical Execution Leadership

Lead end-to-end technical execution for mission package integration on Saronic platforms, from design support through field deployment and sustainment.
Support complex payload and package integrations on Saronic’s 180ft Marauder, while also supporting Corsair and Mirage integration efforts.
Translate high-level requirements into actionable steps for engineering and operations teams, driving disciplined technical execution in ambiguous environments.

Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to interface confidently with technical and non-technical audiences.

Apply a full range of acquisition program management policies and procedures to perform acquisition management activities in support of existing and future F/B Directorate aircraft programs and platforms

Develop and coordinate responses to taskers related to internal and external program inquiries
Support warfighter Urgent Operational Needs (UON) and Joint Urgent Operational Needs (JUON) execution teams by recommending accelerated test concepts, minimum integration levels, and trade-offs among risk, schedule, performance, and cost

Provide inputs, draft, coordinate, adjudicate comments, and produce final coordinated milestone documents and assessments, including staff summary packages for milestone approval
Support requirements document development and the Joint Capabilities Integration and Development System (JCIDS) process and staffing
Translate user requirements documents, including Capability Development Documents (CDDs), Capability Production Documents (CPDs), and CONOPs, into Request for Proposal (RFP) documentation for the F/B Directorate
Support key acquisition events and reviews, including SRRs, PDRs, CDRs, TRRs, TCMs, FCAs, PCAs, PRRs, TIMs, and other applicable reviews
Apply program management initiatives involving commercial items, including Non-Developmental Items (NDI), Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS), and Federal Aviation Administration (FAA)-certified items
Support commercial practices and acquisition approaches such as Performance Based Business Environment (PBBE), Evolutionary Acquisition (EA), Agile Acquisition (AA), JCIDS, CONOPS, partnering, architectural views, and Capabilities Review and Risk Assessment (CRRA)
Assist with Automated Business Services System (ABSS), System Management Analysis Reporting Tool (SMART), and Integrated Budget Documentation and Execution System (IDECS), including producing documents using IDECS
Support DAG processes, including Monthly Acquisition Reports (MARs), Defense Acquisition Executive Summary (DAES), Selected Acquisition Reports (SARs), and the Task Management Tool (TMT)
Plan, coordinate, and participate in integrated program reviews and conferences, including executive, readiness, technical, budget, design, weapon system, requirements working group, supportability, and management reviews

Process and complete Modification Proposal AF Form 1067 activities, including logging, assigning review responsibilities, tracking completions, providing responses to using commands, and archiving results

Support capability planning and development actions, including implementation of policies, processes, and tools, High Powered Team (HPT) support, and capability-based planning processes for AFMC
Support AFMC Capabilities Integration Panel resources, including financial and manpower resources, and review capability requirements and option sets to ensure interoperability and linkages to other capabilities
Communicate across multiple platforms, programs, phases, and enterprises while supporting integration of intelligence information and infrastructure for cross-enterprise capabilities planning and system acquisition
Support establishment of a capability architect function to develop integrated architectures for cross-enterprise comparison, analysis, and integration
Identify and advocate AF Operational Support (OS) capability requirements and support OS transformation through capability-based planning, modernization initiatives, process engineering, and integration of intelligence from concept development through sustainment
Promote the use of Modeling, Simulation, and Analysis (MS&A) throughout the acquisition life cycle and support development and maintenance of common-use MS&A tools
Support command leadership and policy for modeling, simulation, and analysis to enable capability-based planning and acquisition; access modeling databases and perform specific analysis
Plan, organize, and manage critical aspects of the development, production, and/or deployment of capabilities, including systems of systems, families of systems, systems, subsystems, and equipment
Support the Directorate/Division Self-Inspection Program (SIP), including preparing for inspections, distributing checklist information, developing and maintaining checklist tracking/reporting, monitoring completion status, and recommending corrective actions
Prepare, maintain, update, and review test and test-related documentation, including the Test and Evaluation Master Plan (TEMP), Integrated System Test Plan, Integrated Test Team (ITT) Charter, Program Introduction Document (PID), Statement of Capabilities (SOC), and other required test plans and reports
Review test documentation for adequacy, specification/performance requirement compliance, and conformity with mandatory guidance, and provide recommendations for improvement
Recommend, assess, and analyze requirements and objectives, test and evaluation concepts, strategies, and plans
Coordinate acceptance test procedures and associated plans, including testing requirements with program office customers, contractors, and other agencies with standardization requirements for test programs

Requirements

Education, Requirements and Qualifications:

Must have a Secret clearance
Master's or Doctorate Degree in a related field and ten (10) years of experience in the respective technical/professional discipline being performed, five (5) years of which must be in the DoD;

Your work will support defense and health agencies where AI solutions directly contribute to national security and public well-being.

At Northrop Grumman, our employees have incredible opportunities to work on revolutionary systems that impact people's lives around the world today, and for generations to come. Northrop Grumman (NG) is seeking an Industrial Security Manager 3
to lead and manage the sector-wide investigations, insider threat, and counterintelligence program for the Aeronautics Systems Sector. As a key member of the centralized NG Investigations, Insider Threat, and Counterintelligence Team, this role has primary responsibility for that sector while also enabling and supporting aligned investigative and insider threat efforts across the company. The role reports directly to the Corporate Director of Investigations and Insider Threat and serves as a principal advisor to the Aeronautics Sector Senior Security Director, as well as other sector and company leadership. This position is located in M
elbourne, FL OR Palmdale, CA,
and due to the dynamic environment and size of both the sector and the company, domestic and international travel is required.

Primary Responsibilities

Sector & Enterprise Leadership

Provide sector-wide leadership for investigations, insider threat, and counterintelligence activities, set priorities and ensure effective allocation of investigative and analytic resources.
Serve as an enterprise leader and thought partner by helping to shape and implement policies, procedures, workflows, initiatives, and cross-sector teaming efforts.
Develop and maintain procedures, operating standards, and investigative protocols.
Track program performance using key metrics and preparing reports, dashboards, and executive summaries.
Recommend improvements which enhance operational effectiveness, regulatory compliance, and customer service.
Maintain well-established liaison relationships in the investigations, insider threat, and counterintelligence arenas with law enforcement, prosecutorial agencies, and the intelligence community, such as DCSA, FBI, AFOSI, and NCIS.

Enterprise Investigations

Manage the corporate investigations program for the sector, including allegations of insider threat activity, counterintelligence concerns, workplace violence, fraud, misconduct, theft, policy violations, and other security-related incidents.
Lead and oversee investigators and case work to ensure fair, objective, legally defensible investigations and compliance with government, customer, and corporate policies, procedures, and practices.
Conduct and oversee insider threat and counterintelligence investigations consistent with applicable government and corporate protocols.
Collaborate with internal and external stakeholders for investigations and operations.
Review investigative findings, ensure appropriate documentation and evidence preservation, and recommend corrective and preventive actions.
Monitor metrics and trends to identify systemic risks, emerging issues, and opportunities for continuous improvement.

Insider Threat & Risk Management

Lead and administer the sector’s Insider Threat Program, while helping to shape and inform the company’s overall insider threat program through data, gap and trend analysis, and operational insights.
Monitor and analyze security incidents and investigative trends to identify emerging risks, including insider threats.
Develop and implement strategies to address potential threats, risks, and vulnerabilities.

Security & Compliance

Oversee investigations of security complaints and compliance concerns while ensuring consistent application of company policies, procedures, and standards.
Interpret, apply, and ensure adherence to federal security regulations that govern company operations, including the National Industrial Security Program Operating Manual (NISPOM), DOD Manual 5205.07 Special Access Program Security Manual, Federal Acquisition Regulations (FAR), and other applicable directives.
Monitor regulatory changes and assist with updates to policies, procedures, and compliance programs.

Training & Awareness

Develop and deliver security education and awareness, and implement corporate investigations, insider threat, and counterintelligence programs across cleared and uncleared facilities.

Stakeholder & Agency Partnerships

Build collaborative relationships across the sector and company to ensure aligned decision-making and consistent execution.
Partner closely with Ethics, Labor and Employment, Employee Relations, Cybersecurity, Human Resources, Legal, Compliance, security counterparts, business leaders, and relevant government agencies (e.g., DCSA) to identify and mitigate company risks and insider threats, strengthen compliance, and protect company assets.
Coordinate information sharing between internal stakeholders and external law enforcement and government entities to support security investigations and broader security objectives, partnering with Legal as appropriate.
Support government reporting requirements and regulatory inquiries, in coordination with internal stakeholders and government partners.

People Leadership

Build, lead, and develop a high-performing team responsible for investigations, insider threat, and counterintelligence.
Lead, mentor, and develop team members fostering a culture of integrity, accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
Model and promote a self‑starter culture grounded in uncompromising integrity and ethical behavior in all activities.
Establish team priorities, assign work, and monitor workload, quality, and performance.
Support workforce planning, hiring, onboarding, performance management, and employee development.
Represent the team effectively with senior leadership and other stakeholders through clear briefings, written reports, and executive-ready communications.
Demonstrate strong interpersonal skills and a highly collaborative, team-oriented leadership style, with the ability to build trust, influence without authority, and work effectively across diverse stakeholder groups.

Job Summary

The Manager, Information Security is responsible for strengthening and maintaining an organization's overall information security posture. This role provides leadership across security governance, risk and compliance, and security operations while partnering with IT teams and business leadership to identify and mitigate security risks. The position will oversee security technologies, operational processes, compliance initiatives, and technical security personnel to ensure the organization maintains effective protections across its network, systems, identities, applications, and cloud environments.

Key Responsibilities

Develop, maintain, and improve information security policies, procedures, standards, and governance processes.
Lead security risk management activities, including threat intelligence, risk assessments, risk analysis, and mitigation planning.
Manage security compliance programs, including ISO 27001, ISO 27701, PCI-DSS, client assessments, audits, and security questionnaires.
Oversee security resources, budgets, vendors, and managed security service providers.
Lead security awareness and training initiatives and advise IT, leadership, and business teams regarding emerging threats, policies, controls, and security best practices.
Review security architecture and designs for network, systems, applications, identity, collaboration, and cloud infrastructure.
Manage ongoing security monitoring, testing, audits, remediation activities, and compliance tracking.

Provide leadership and oversight for security technologies and operational functions, including firewalls, network segmentation, vulnerability management, privileged and remote access, EDR/NGAV, SIEM, email security, and continuous monitoring.
Lead and prioritize security projects, administrative initiatives, and continuous improvement efforts.
Manage, mentor, and develop technical security engineering personnel.
Collaborate with IT, business leadership, and other stakeholders to identify security requirements and implement appropriate controls.
Maintain strict confidentiality of sensitive organizational, client, employee, and business information.

Minimum Education & Experience Requirements

Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Cybersecurity, Computer Science, or a related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience.
Minimum of 10 years of experience in information technology, including at least 5 years of information security-related experience.
At least 3 years of experience managing technical security engineers or similar security-focused personnel.
Strong IT operations background with experience in networking, systems administration, infrastructure, software development, or related technical disciplines.
Demonstrated experience implementing and maintaining ISO 27001 and ISO 27701 programs.
Experience managing security governance, risk, compliance, and operational security functions.

CISSP, CISM, CEH, CIPP, or comparable security certification is highly desirable.
Candidates currently pursuing relevant professional certifications may be considered.
Ability to maintain strict confidentiality and appropriately handle sensitive organizational and personnel information.
Willingness and ability to travel to other organizational offices or locations as required.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

Strong knowledge of information security principles, practices, frameworks, and industry standards.
Thorough understanding of security threats involving systems, networks, identities, applications, and cloud services.
Working knowledge of security technologies, including firewalls, SIEM, EDR/NGAV, vulnerability management, network segmentation, identity and privileged access management, email security, and security monitoring tools.
Strong understanding of security governance, risk management, compliance, auditing, and remediation processes.
Ability to assess technical risks and clearly communicate their business impact to non-technical stakeholders.
Strong leadership, team management, coaching, and mentoring capabilities.
Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making skills.

Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Ability to collaborate effectively with technical teams, business leaders, vendors, and other stakeholders.

Experience working within a law firm, professional services organization, financial services organization, or similarly highly regulated environment.
Experience managing security programs across multiple offices or geographically distributed environments.
Experience working with client security assessments, third-party risk reviews, and external audits.
Experience with cloud security architecture and identity security.

Demonstrated ability to lead organizational security improvements and mature existing security programs.

Primarily professional office and technology operations environment within the Pittsburgh regional area.
May require occasional travel to other organizational offices or locations.

Regular interaction with IT personnel, organizational leadership, vendors, and business stakeholders.

Familiarity with the sixteen standard divisions of construction and knowledge of technical listening devices commonly used by foreign intelligence services is required.

Valid certificates for successful completion of a 32-Hour or greater Site Security Manager Training Course and a 40-Hour or greater Construction Surveillance Technician Training Course are mandatory.
