new_jobs.title: Principal, Strategy and Operations Manager - GBSG U.S. Marketing
new_jobs.description:
Overview

Intuit is a mission-driven, global financial platform company that gives everyone the opportunity to prosper. We do this by using technology to solve our customers’ most important problems. We serve customers by finding more ways to put more money in their pockets, eliminating work and drudgery so they can focus on their lives and what matters to them, and ensuring that every financial decision that they make, they make it with confidence. We are also at an important point in Intuit’s transformation, as AI and human intelligence reshape both the experiences we deliver for customers and how we operate. Across GBSG, that means making sharper choices about where we invest, how we grow, and how we move with greater speed and focus.

As a Principal Strategy and Operations Manager, you will sit at the center of Commercial Operations, the connective tissue between strategy and execution across the commercial organization. You'll own the planning rhythm, drive the initiatives that unlock growth and profitability, and turn ambiguous business problems into decisions leadership can act on. Working at the intersection of business strategy, data analysis, and AI-enabled operations, you'll partner closely with finance, marketing, sales, and product to translate priorities into measurable outcomes and to build the operating cadence that keeps them on track. Be part of a high-growth environment where your contributions have direct, visible impact. We are looking for a strategic operator who is an avid learner, experimenter, and builder, ready to rewire how Commercial Operations runs in the AI era.

Responsibilities

Strategic Planning and Execution: Develop and execute key business initiatives to drive growth and profitability. Own and evolve the quarterly and annual planning process, helping leaders make explicit choices about priorities, investments, tradeoffs and sequencing. Use AI-assisted tools to compress cycle time and get to decisions faster.
Project Management and Cross-functional Collaboration: Manage strategic initiatives from conception to execution, collaborating with finance, marketing, sales, and product teams to ensure alignment and effective implementation. Identify and drive mitigation strategies, prioritize initiatives, and ensure alignment with cross-functional leaders to assess effectiveness and make necessary adjustments.
Performance and Data Analysis: Identify and recommend improvements to processes and systems, conducting in-depth analyses of business performance, market trends, and operational metrics to enhance efficiency and inform strategic decisions. Use AI and automation to expand the scope and speed of analysis, and to automate recurring reporting so effort shifts from data assembly to insight.
Executive Communication: Shape executive decisions by distilling complex analysis and data into clear recommendations, alternatives, and tradeoffs. Communicate those insights through crisp presentations, written narratives, and other executive-ready materials that create the clarity and alignment leaders need to make decisions and move.
AI Enablement and Velocity: Bring a demonstrated track record of using AI to meaningfully increase personal and team throughput. Design changes that address root causes rather than adding another process or layer.

Qualifications

This role demands a blend of analytical prowess, operational expertise, and leadership skills to drive effective business strategies and operational efficiencies in a complex and evolving environment.

7+ years of experience in strategy consulting, business operations, or a related field, ideally with experience in management consulting or large technology companies.
Experience leading multi-year strategy and planning, including long-range planning, annual planning, scenario development, and translating strategy into operating priorities.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with experience in data analysis, financial modeling, and KPI trend analysis. Proficiency in SQL, Python or similar for data analysis and automation scripting; experience with no‑code/low‑code platforms (e.g., Cursor, Claude Code); a plus.
Track record of working cross‑functionally with product, engineering, data scientists, and marketing channel owners. Understanding of marketing measurement, incrementality testing, and performance metrics.
Excellent verbal, written, and presentation skills. Ability to develop clear and impactful reports and presentations for stakeholders. Demonstrated leadership abilities with experience influencing and building partnerships across all levels of an organization.
Proven ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously, with strong organizational and time management skills. Comfortable working in a dynamic, high-growth environment with ambiguity.
Bachelor’s degree in Data Science, Finance, Engineering, Economics, Business, or a related field; advanced degree such as an MBA preferred.

Footer

Intuit provides a competitive compensation package with a strong pay for performance rewards approach. This position may be eligible for a cash bonus, equity rewards and benefits, in accordance with our applicable plans and programs (see more about our compensation and benefits at Intuit®: Careers | Benefits). Pay offered is based on factors such as job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and work location. To drive ongoing fair pay for employees, Intuit conducts regular comparisons across categories of ethnicity and gender.

The Expected Base Pay Range For This Position Is

Mountain View $197,000 - $266,000

New York $190,000- $257,000

San Diego, CA $196,000- $265,000

Benefits

Description

The Manager, Business Operations is responsible for the financial planning, operational oversight, and business management of an assigned clinic section. This role oversees budget development and monitoring, financial reporting, and operational analysis to support the section’s strategic and financial objectives.

The position partners closely with section leadership and finance teams to ensure sound financial management, operational efficiency, and compliance with organizational policies, regulatory requirements, and financial reporting standards. This role also supervises staff and supports process improvements that strengthen financial performance and operational effectiveness.

Responsibilities

RESPONSIBILITIES
Financial Planning & Budget Management

Develop, administer, and monitor section operating and capital budgets.
Support annual budget development, financial forecasting, and long- term financial planning.
Analyze financial data to inform business objectives and departmental strategy.
Monitor capital equipment, operational, and personnel budgets to ensure fiscal accountability.
Review prior budget expenditures, investigate variances, and recommend corrective actions.
Provide budget recommendations and financial guidance to section leadership.
Work closely with the clinic Finance department to ensure alignment with financial policies and procedures.

Financial Reporting & Analysis

Prepare operational, financial, and statistical reports for leadership and regulatory agencies.
Maintain accurate accounting and statistical records for financial programs.
Collect, organize, and analyze financial and operational data to produce management reports.
Utilize financial systems ( FAS) and resource tools to reconcile accounts and analyze financial performance.
Prepare journal entries, accruals, fiscal year audit schedules, and asset depreciation documentation.
Support financial systems and reporting tools used for operational and financial reporting.

Grants, Contracts & Financial Compliance

Ensure awarded grants comply with established budget parameters and financial guidelines.
Forecast financial needs related to grant funding increases, changes, and awards.
Negotiate new and renewal service contracts and review vendor agreements for compliance with organizational requirements.
Interpret financial regulations and implement appropriate auditing, filing, and compliance procedures.

Operational Leadership & Process Improvement

Oversee and improve financial and operational procedures within the assigned section.
Coordinate financial analysis initiatives and data collection activities across the department.
Participate in the development of section goals, objectives, and operational strategies.
Lead or support projects aimed at improving operational efficiency, such as facility planning, staffing restructures, or service expansion.

Staff Leadership & Development

Supervise staff and manage employee performance.
Provide coaching, training, and ongoing performance feedback.
Monitor workflow, assign responsibilities, and ensure operational productivity.
Assist with workforce planning, recruitment, interviewing, and hiring decisions.
Support employee relations and provide input on compensation, benefits, and personnel matters.

Policy Administration & Compliance

Administer departmental policies, procedures, and forms in compliance with state, federal, and organizational regulations.
Review, revise, and communicate policies to ensure regulatory compliance.
Advise managers and staff on the effective administration of financial and operational policies.

Administrative & Organizational Support

Coordinate preparation and processing of employee documentation, employment requisitions, and departmental paperwork.
Develop and implement improved data collection and reporting methods.
Conduct training sessions to ensure consistent financial and operational practices.
Participate in professional development and continuing education activities.
Perform additional duties as assigned.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

Education

Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, Healthcare Administration, or a related field required.

Experience

Three ( 3) to five ( 5) years of professional business or management experience required, preferably in a healthcare setting.
Minimum of two ( 2) years of supervisory or management experience required.

Preferred

Master’s degree or fellowship may substitute for required experience.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS: 1-10 lbs 0-33% of the work day (occasionally), negligible 34-66% of the workday (frequently), negligible 67-100% of the workday (constantly). Lifting 10 lbs max, carrying of small articles such as dockets, ledgers, files, small tools, occasional standing & walking, frequent sitting, close eye work (computers, typing, reading, writing), Physical demands may vary depending on assigned work area and work tasks.

ENVIRONMENTAL FACTORS: Factors affecting environment conditions may vary depending on the assigned work area and tasks. new_jobs.title: Supply Chain Program Manager
new_jobs.description:
Job Description

The Manager I – Supply Chain supports ship repair, modernization, overhaul, and conversion projects through leadership of procurement activities, subcontract management, and material readiness. This position also functions as a Supply Chain Program Manager (SCPM) operating under the Director of Supply Chain. In this capacity, the SCPM assists in program‑level planning, performance monitoring, and compliance activities, while serving as the primary interface with Ships Management for subcontractor performance on the deck plate. The manager leads the Material Production Coordinators and ensures material availability in accordance with the Master Material Index to support production timelines.

Key Responsibilities

Lead and supervise Material Production Coordinators, ensuring material coordination, kitting, staging, and availability in alignment with the Master Material Index and production milestones.
Assist the Director of Supply Chain in developing, maintaining, and executing supply chain strategies supporting ship repair programs, including demand forecasting, procurement planning, and risk identification.
Serve as the primary supply chain interface with Ships Management for overseeing subcontractor performance on the deck plate, ensuring quality, schedule adherence, and compliance with contractual requirements.
Support the Director of Supply Chain in communicating supply chain readiness, issues, risks, and performance to program and executive teams.
Contribute to the development and maintenance of the Supply Chain Program Plan (SCPP) and participate in integrated reviews.
Conduct Bill of Material analysis, costing, planning, and non‑labor cost development; support financial and estimating activities for ongoing and future projects.
Review requisitions for accuracy and compliance, monitor non‑labor performance metrics, and help develop cost models and program status updates.
Collaborate with proposal management, estimating, program management, engineering, planning, and production to interpret specifications and convert requirements into procurement strategies and material readiness plans.
Assist supply chain coordinators and analysts with sourcing, evaluation, negotiation, selection, and contractual management of subcontractors and material suppliers to ensure alignment with specifications, quality, budget, schedule, and earned value requirements.
Ensure subcontract documentation alignment with customer regulations, including FAR, DFARS, NAVSEA standards, and applicable commercial maritime requirements.
Participate in establishing supplier milestone objectives and support monitoring supplier performance to schedules and contractual specifications.
Drive continuous improvement initiatives focused on procurement efficiency, supplier reliability, subcontractor deck plate performance, and overall program material readiness.

Required Education, Experience, & Skills

Typically Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Technology, Supply Chain Management, or Operations.

At Docebo, we’re using AI to change how people learn at work—and we mean actually change it. But our real mission goes deeper: we help teams move faster, work smarter, and focus on the work that truly matters. Our platform is built with intelligent, time-saving tools that personalize learning, eliminate busywork, and turn training from a checkbox into a superpower. The result? Better experiences for learners and real results for businesses.

We’re shaping the future of learning with a team that isn’t afraid to challenge the status quo. If you're excited by the idea of using AI to make work-life better for real people–you’ll feel right at home here. And it’s not just what we build, it’s how we show up. At Docebo, our values aren’t just posters on the wall—they guide how we work every day. We call it the Docebo Heart
: trust by default, assume positive intent, and create space for different perspectives to thrive.

So… what are you waiting for? Join 900+ Docebians around the world and help us reinvent the way people learn, because learning never stops.

The Adventure Ahead 🚀

Our Salesforce team is at the center of how Docebo sells, renews, and serves customers. We're investing in how it operates, and this is a net-new role we're adding to lead that change. We have strong senior technical talent on the team — what we're adding is a product owner who can set direction, manage stakeholders, and give that talent well-scoped work to build.

You'll own the backlog and the priorities. You'll define the intake and process the team runs on. And you'll work shoulder-to-shoulder with our senior architects and admins as an advisor and partner — not to out-engineer them, but to make sure the team is solving the right problems in the right order, with the business bought in.

The Day-to-Day 🛠️

The product backlog and priorities. Turn business needs into clear problem statements, user stories, and acceptance criteria. Prioritize with stakeholders so the team always knows what's next and why.
Stakeholder management. Be the connective tissue between the Salesforce team and the business — Revenue Operations, Marketing, and Finance. Manage expectations, negotiate trade-offs, and bring the team into solution design early instead of receiving pre-baked requests.
Process and ways of working. Define and stand up how the team intakes, prioritizes, and delivers work. Set the standard for a good request and make it stick, so work enters the team ready to build.
Partnership with senior technical leads. Work with the team's architects and admins as an advisor and thought partner. You bring the product and process lens; they own the technical design. Together you keep the org healthy and the roadmap realistic.
AI-driven innovation. Champion how the team uses AI to work smarter — from AI-assisted ticket triage and intake scoring to identifying where automation and AI can improve how Docebo runs on Salesforce.
A seat at the table. Represent the Salesforce team when the business evaluates new tools, so decisions that affect the platform are made deliberately, not discovered later.

Your Superpowers ⚡

Platform Depth: Proven experience as a Salesforce Architect, Senior Admin, or Business Analyst with the hands-on expertise needed to speak fluent platform and earn instant respect with technical leads.
Product Ownership Mastery: Strong track record of running backlogs, scoping airtight requirements, prioritizing high-value features, and confidently saying "no" with strategic reasoning.
Stakeholder Diplomacy: Exceptional ability to align competing business priorities across departments, negotiate trade-offs with senior leadership, and keep everyone bought into the plan.
Process Architecture: Demonstrated success building lightweight, effective operating frameworks that bring structure and clarity to team workflows without adding bureaucratic bloat.
Impactful Communication: Talent for translating technical complexities into business-friendly language for executives while keeping developers clear on the mission and priorities.
AI-Forward Mindset: Natural curiosity and drive to leverage emerging AI solutions to optimize team operations and CRM efficiency.
Governance Savvy: Deep comfort navigating regulated environments, including SOX controls, structured deployment schedules, and strict UAT standards.

Bonus Points 🌟

Certified Expertise: Holding active Salesforce certifications (e.g., Administrator, Platform App Builder, or Architect track credentials).
RevOps Synergy: Direct experience acting as the designated product owner partnering with a fast-paced Revenue Operations organization.
Revenue Cloud Knowledge: Hands-on familiarity with Salesforce Revenue Cloud (CPQ/Billing) or leading complex billing system migrations.
Applied AI Experience: Practical background implementing AI-driven workflows or tools within CRM or delivery environments.

Great work can happen anywhere but coming together helps us go further. Our team spends three days a week in the office (Tuesday-Thursday) to collaborate, solve problems, and learn from each other. With flexibility the rest of the week, it’s a balance designed to help everyone do their best work and keep growing.

Our Total Rewards Philosophy
🎉

Rewarding Impact: We lead with competitive pay to reward the impact, skills and traits that fuel our success.
Fostering Holistic Wellbeing: We care deeply about and invest in the whole person with programs that support our people’s physical, mental, and financial well-being.
Empowering Our Talent Culture: We build a culture of trust and empowerment by designing our rewards and benefits with transparency, equity, and flexibility, enabling our people to do their best work and stay for the long haul.

Family First: We provide coverage offering you time with your little one(s) so you can soak up all those precious moments. Fun fact: we had 30 Docebian babies join the family in 2025!

At Docebo, we create seamless, AI-powered learning experiences for over 3,000 customers worldwide. Mastercard powers economies and empowers people in 200+ countries and territories worldwide. Together with our customers, we’re helping build a sustainable economy where everyone can prosper. We support a wide range of digital payments choices, making transactions secure, simple, smart and accessible. Our technology and innovation, partnerships and networks combine to deliver a unique set of products and services that help people, businesses and governments realize their greatest potential.

Title And Summary

Senior Threat Intelligence Analyst

Who is Mastercard?

Mastercard is a global technology company in the payments industry. Our mission is to connect and power an inclusive, digital economy that benefits everyone, everywhere by making transactions safe, simple, smart, and accessible. Using secure data and networks, partnerships and passion, our innovations and solutions help individuals, financial institutions, governments, and businesses realize their greatest potential.

Our decency quotient, or DQ, drives our culture and everything we do inside and outside of our company. With connections across more than 210 countries and territories, we are building a sustainable world that unlocks priceless possibilities for all.

Overview

Mastercard is seeking a Threat Intelligence Analyst to join the Mastercard Intelligence Center. This role will focus on gathering, analyzing, and reporting on cyber, physical, and geopolitical threats targeting Mastercard. The ideal candidate will have 5-8 years of experience in intelligence collection, analysis, production, and briefing, and will act as a liaison between internal Corporate Security teams, Mastercard technology teams, and external partners.

Key responsibilities include tracking Advanced Persistent Threat (APT) actors, leveraging Open-Source Intelligence (OSINT) techniques, and identifying threats to Mastercard’s infrastructure. The analyst will also support mitigation efforts, explore opportunities for automation, and contribute to continuous process improvements.

Collect, process, analyze, publish, and disseminate threat intelligence for Mastercard
Leverage that intelligence to threat-inform risk-based decisions across the organization
Author risk assessments that capture threat landscape impacts to business operations
Brief intelligence analysis to internal stakeholders
Partner with internal stakeholders, principally the SOC, Vulnerability Management, Fraud Prevention, Regional Security, and Crisis Management to fuse intelligence from across the organization
Partner with external stakeholders such as government departments, law enforcement, intelligence agencies, and industry to enable threat intelligence sharing across public and private partners
Support threat scenario development for red teaming, exercising, and resilience testing

All About You

Possesses a strong analytical mindset with experience collecting, evaluating, and synthesizing intelligence from diverse sources.
Demonstrates solid understanding of intelligence tradecraft, including structured analytic techniques, threat modeling, and risk assessment methodologies.
Bachelor’s or Master’s Degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Digital Forensics, Cybersecurity, Telecommunications, or Information Assurance.
5-8 years of experience as an intelligence analyst with a strong foundation in critical thinking and the intelligence cycle.
Broad understanding of networking and enterprise IT systems.
Has experience monitoring threat activity and translating complex information into clear, actionable intelligence products for technical and non-technical audiences.
Communicates effectively in writing and verbally, with the ability to brief senior leaders and cross-functional stakeholders with clarity and confidence.
Demonstrates sound judgment, curiosity, and a proactive approach to identifying threats and informing risk-based decisions.
Experience working in a global team or within a Follow-the-Sun operational model.

new_jobs.description:
About AlphaSense

The world’s most sophisticated companies rely on AlphaSense to remove uncertainty from decision-making. With market intelligence and search built on proven AI, AlphaSense delivers insights that matter from content you can trust. Our universe of public and private content includes equity research, company filings, event transcripts, expert calls, news, trade journals, and clients’ own research content.

The acquisition of Tegus by AlphaSense in 2024 advances our shared mission to empower professionals to make smarter decisions through AI-driven market intelligence. Our platform is trusted by over 6,000 enterprise customers, including a majority of the S&P 500. Founded in 2011, AlphaSense is headquartered in New York City with more than 2,000 employees across the globe and offices in the U.S., U.K., Finland, India, Singapore, Canada, and Ireland. Come join us!

Remote within Canada, able to work in the Pacific time zone

About The Role

We are hiring Security Operations Analyst II
to join our Security Operations team in a fully remote capacity from Canada. This role sits at Tier 1–2 in our operating model — you are past the stage of learning what alerts look like and ready to own triage, perform structured investigations, and contribute to detection quality. You will handle the day-to-day alert queue, investigate escalated or ambiguous cases, handle incidents and work closely with senior analysts and the Security Operations Manager to close coverage gaps.

We expect you to think analytically, document thoroughly, and operate with growing independence. You will be supported by experienced colleagues and a mature toolset, but you are expected to bring real investigative instinct and a curiosity to grow to the role from day one.

What You Will Do

Alert Triage & Investigation

Monitor and triage alerts across endpoint, network, cloud, runtime and identity data sources with accuracy and appropriate urgency
Perform structured investigations on escalated or ambiguous alerts: pivot across log sources, correlate events, and build a coherent timeline
Classify alerts correctly — true positive, false positive, or benign — with documented rationale, not just a verdict
Identify scope and blast radius on confirmed incidents: affected users, systems, and data before escalating or containing
Escalate to senior analysts with a complete investigation package — context, evidence, timeline, and a hypothesis

Incident Response Support

Participate in active incident response under senior analyst or manager direction: evidence collection, log pulls, timeline reconstruction
Execute containment actions — endpoint isolation, account suspension, token revocation — as directed with documented rationale
Maintain accurate and timely case documentation throughout the incident lifecycle
Contribute to post-incident timelines and assist with root cause documentation

Cloud & Identity Security Monitoring

Monitor cloud audit logs and native threat detection findings for suspicious IAM activity, unusual API calls, and access anomalies
Investigate identity provider events: suspicious logins, MFA bypass attempts, session anomalies, and unauthorized app assignments
Recognize common cloud-native attack patterns: credential abuse via metadata service, privilege escalation via IAM role assumption, and storage misconfiguration access
Correlate cloud-side events with endpoint and network telemetry to build a fuller picture of attacker activity

Detection & Quality Improvement

Flag false positives and noisy detections with enough context for a senior analyst or detection engineer to tune them
Identify gaps in existing detection coverage based on alert patterns you observe during triage
Apply knowledge of MITRE ATT&CK to label attacker techniques and communicate findings consistently
Contribute to runbook accuracy by flagging outdated steps or missing guidance encountered during investigations
Participate with Detections Engineers to build detections and contribute to automating activity with an Engineering mindset

Documentation & Communication

Write clear, concise case notes that a colleague could pick up mid-investigation without needing to re-investigate from scratch
Produce shift handoff summaries that accurately represent open cases, pending actions, and investigation status
Communicate incident updates to the Security Operations Manager with sufficient clarity to brief upward without re-investigation

Required

WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

2–4+ years of hands-on experience in a SOC, or security operations role with direct alert triage responsibility
Solid understanding of the MITRE ATT&CK framework — you use it to label and communicate attacker behavior, not just reference it
Working knowledge of EDR tooling: process tree analysis, behavioral detection review, and basic endpoint artifact interpretation
Familiarity with SIEM-based investigation: querying logs, correlating events across sources, and building timelines from normalized data
Understanding of foundational network protocols (TCP/IP, DNS, HTTP/S, TLS) and how attackers abuse them
Exposure to cloud security monitoring ex. AWS or GCP — including audit log review and IAM-related alert investigation
Experience investigating identity-based alerts in an enterprise identity provider (e.g., Okta, Entra ID, or equivalent)
Strong written communication: your case notes are accurate, structured, and useful to someone who wasn’t there

Preferred

Experience with next-gen EDR platforms (e.g., CrowdStrike Falcon, SentinelOne, or equivalent) beyond basic alert review — RTR, process trees, custom detections
Hands-on SIEM experience with a cloud-native platform (e.g., Google SecOps/Chronicle, Microsoft Sentinel, or equivalent)
Exposure to CSPM or cloud security tooling (e.g., Wiz, Prisma Cloud, or equivalent) as an investigation data source
Familiarity with AWS IR fundamentals: CloudTrail, GuardDuty, VPC Flow Logs, IAM chain analysis
Understanding of encoding vs. encryption vs. hashing and their relevance to attacker obfuscation techniques
Experience working alongside or receiving escalations from a managed detection and response (MDR) partner
Relevant certifications: CompTIA CySA+, Security+, BTL1, GCIH, or equivalent practical security credential

Important Application Submission Information

More than a career - a chance to make a difference in people's lives.

Build an exciting, rewarding career with us – help us make a difference for millions of people every day. Consider joining the Duke Energy team, where you'll find a friendly work environment, opportunities for growth and development, recognition for your work, and competitive pay and benefits.

The preferred location is Plainfield, Noblesville, or Huntington. The manager will consider locations in the Northern Indiana Region. The exact location will be determined at the time of offer based on business needs.

This position manages, inspects, and protects a designated portion of the approximate 33,000 miles of purchased easement and fee owned Transmission corridors to ensure customers, contractors, and developers are in compliance with the established AP guidelines. The position collaborates with and presents guidelines to stakeholders and customers and participates in the decision making of the release of transmission easements and selling of fee owned property. In performing the duties, this position must review technical engineering drawings and site plans to ensure that customers, contractors, and developers comply with Duke Energy's guidelines and recorded property rights documents. Engineering plan reviews require a general knowledge of engineering standards, construction standards and techniques, future transmission planning, OSHA rules, NESC rules, as well as other applicable rules. Duties also include the removal of existing encroachments and execution of relevant encroachment agreements. The job requires legal involvement in which the position must be able to maintain detailed documentation, read and interpret legal documents, give depositions, and testify in a court of law.

Depending upon the desired qualifications of the successful applicant, the hiring manager may elect to fill this position at a higher level within the job hierarchy

Responsibilities:

Resolves existing encroachments & Helicopter Reports of encroachments.
This involves negotiating with customers, reviewing, and effectively communicating to customers Duke’s legal rights while pursuing an appropriate course of action.
In some cases, will involve court action and testifying and will require an empathic approach.
Collaborate with observer during Helicopter flight.
Reviews and approves technical engineering drawings (site plans, grading, utilities, landscaping, etc.) to ensure compliance to Duke Energy’s transmission guidelines.
This includes evaluating grade changes to protect and ensure the National Electric Safety Code issues, OSHA minimum approach distances, and Duke Energy minimum clearance standards are not violated.
Meets with developers, architects, engineers, corporate executives, governmental leaders, and lawyers to prevent and resolve encroachment issues created during the plan reviews above.
Prepares professional letters to property owners outlining plan review findings.
Document – detailed conversations, site visits, emails, etc., to support potential review by management or legal team for court action.
With Management oversight, this involves negotiating with customers, reviewing, and effectively communicating Duke’s legal rights to customers while pursuing and recommending an appropriate course of action.
In some cases, this will involve court action and testifying.
Meets with developers, architects, engineers, corporate executives, governmental leaders, and lawyers to resolve encroachment issues that are not resolved at the employee level.
Train, onboard and mentor new employees
Responds to customers and community concerns associated with our AP Programs
Identifies and assigns opportunities for Asset Protection team members to meet with influential leaders to develop a relationship that enhances our ability to prevent encroachments.
Evaluates, recommends, and attends conferences of Professional Land Surveyors, Home Builders, Professional Engineers and Grading Contractors Associations, etc. that are most effective for Asset Protection to attend each year.
Works with government agencies, including DOT and Environmental to ensure compliance with appropriate state and federal regulations and proactive communications of area vegetation management plans and procedures to community stakeholders.
This includes meeting with City/County Planning Boards, Architectural & Engineering Firms, major developers of commercial and residential developments and others who have the ability to encroach on transmission easements.
Assists with activities for escalated projects across the enterprise.
Monitor the performance of contract resources to assure safe work practices, asset protection procedures/standards adherence, and productivity consistent with Duke Energy Expectations
Assist the Lead AP Program Manager as needed for effective coordination and participation during emergency storm operations.
Works with minimal supervision on complex issues
Applying advanced knowledge and problem-solving skills to wide-ranging issues
Integrates industry knowledge related to data into everyday business practices and decision making.
Manages expenditures within region and area of responsibility to ensure that budget target and forecast changes are met.
Implement adjustments within region and area of responsibility to complete necessary work while meeting budget forecasts, including forecast changes.
Participates in and may be required to testify in court issues (meetings with property owner council, depositions, and trial)
Provide and assist in the collection of legal documentation in preparation for any Asset Protection legal action to give depositions or testify in court concerning unresolved encroachment issues.
Coordinates the accumulation of supporting evidence, documenting the case from the beginning to support legal action.

Bachelor's degree in communications, Forestry, Engineering, Real Estate, Business other related discipline
In lieu of associate degree High School Diploma/GED and seven (7) years minimum related work experience.
Valid Driver's License

Demonstrated effective communication and customer relation skills, both verbal and written, including strong presentation skills

Demonstrated ability to work independently and is a self motivator, self initiator, and is able to make decisions and supervise/self manage
Demonstrated ability to read engineering plans

Demonstrated familiarity with NESC & OSHA requirements for the electric business

Demonstrated ability to implement asset protection methods, processes and procedures and train and develop other AP Specialists in the implementation of the same

WHO ARE WE?

Dexterra (part of Dexterra Group) is a fast-growing, financially strong, publicly listed company (TSX:DXT). We have a far-reaching presence across the entire continent North America with hundreds of full-time and part-time opportunities at any given time. We aim to provide our people with more than just a job – we offer fulfilling opportunities in a culture that promotes stability, diversity and inclusion, camaraderie, employee recognition, work-life balance, and doing what you love. For over 75 years, the companies that began independently, and now form Dexterra Group, have been dedicated to serving North American clients to create and manage built environments that play a vital role in our economy and our local communities. And, that’s something we’re truly proud of. Work That Matters, People Who Care.

Job Description

WHAT'S THE JOB?

Reporting to the Operations Manager, liaising with the Director and Senior Manager HSE (health, safety, and environment), the HSE and Security Manager is responsible for effectively championing the HSE systems in order to maintain and improve upon our best-in-class HSE performance. The HSE and Security Manager will be responsible for planning, executing, and facilitating HSE policy and procedure compliance, working at site to ensure consistent level of performance, and strengthening lines of communication. The HSE and Security Manager, will be tasked with ensuring that HSE is scalable to accommodate anticipated growth and has a heightened profile in line with all strategic objectives of the business. In addition, the HSE and Security Manager will provide oversight and management of site security operations for the workforce accommodation , ensuring the protection of residents, staff, visitors, company assets, and facilities. This includes ensuring security protocols, access control measures, emergency response procedures, and contractor security requirements are consistently implemented and maintained in alignment with company standards and client expectations.

Key Responsibilities

Manage and otherwise support the safety practices, policies, procedures, and plans of the company.
Responsible for the overall management and leadership of HSE programs, in support of the Dexterra Group HSE direction.
Provide necessary training, leadership, support, and control to meet the company’s goals of preventing work-related physical and psychosocial injuries and illnesses, provide safe and healthy workplaces, protecting the natural environment.

Support business development with required HSE documentation.
Support HSE performance to achieve targeted business output and improvement levels.
Support and/or otherwise implement new HSE initiatives, opportunities, and promotions in consultation with the Director and Senior Manager HSE
Ensure operational teams are aware of HSEQ communications and publications.
Provide direction to management and supervisors in the investigation and incident management process, including workers compensation claims, with the focus on Root Cause and prevention measures.
Conducting assessments and provide recommendations, using technical, human factors and other theoretical knowledge, to research, review and interpret information on hazards to identify causation, consequences, possible risk controls, including critical controls.
Support annual audits for maintenance of ISO certification.
Maintain current knowledge of local, state, and federal HSE codes, regulations, laws, and other relevant standards.
Engage with regulatory agencies and supporting operations with corrective actions from regulatory visits.
Update employees and management on current HSE industry topics/trends.
Work together with the other members of the HSEQ team to support and improve the HSE management system.
Accept authority to take any necessary action to maintain overall safe practices and procedures, including the authority to cease an unsafe operating procedure and to instill the same expectation within others.
Support management to ensure all equipment and buildings owned or operated by the company comply with safety and fire regulations and any other state or Federal regulations.
Engaging with contractors and supporting contractor evaluations
Supporting operations with applicable electronic systems.
Manage all security programs and activities within the Maverick Workforce Accommodation site, ensuring compliance with company, client, and regulatory requirements.
Oversee site access control systems, visitor management processes, and physical security measures.
Supervise and support security personnel and contractors, ensuring effective performance, training, and compliance with site standards.
Conduct security risk assessments and develop mitigation strategies to protect people, property, and operations.
Investigate security incidents, breaches, thefts, and other related events and ensure corrective actions are implemented.
Collaborate with site operations, client representatives, emergency services, and regulatory agencies on security-related matters.
Ensure emergency response, evacuation, and business continuity plans incorporate security requirements and are regularly tested.
Monitor security trends and emerging risks and implement continuous improvement initiatives to strengthen site security.
Support workforce accommodation operations by ensuring a safe, secure, and welcoming environment for residents, employees, contractors, and visitors.
Conduct regular audits and inspections of security systems, procedures, and contractor performance.
Other duties as required.

Undergraduate Degree in Health & Safety, Science, Public Health or equivalent.
CSP or international equivalent
Auditing certifications are an asset e.g. ISO or Environmental Auditing
Valid First Aid, working at heights certifications are an asset
Must possess a valid driver’s license and be flexible to travel.
Desirable trait background in Military and/or Law enforcement
5+ years’ experience in health, safety, or environment.
5+ years managing people
Completion of OHSA 30 training is an asset

Opportunity to lead a large-scale workforce accommodation operation
Key leadership role with direct impact on performance and client satisfaction

Strong focus on safety, quality, and continuous improvement

Evaluate warfighting gap technical solutions using MOEs/MOPs across warfare areas and quantifiably prioritize their suitability and feasibility.
Conducts statistical trend analysis on sensor, systems, weapon and countermeasure data across warfare areas and ascertain system performance against warfighting requirements.
Investigates the validity of probabilistic models and algorithms manifesting as capabilities in proposed warfighting gap solutions.
Ensures the design and execution of M&S studies meet the specified objectives.
Communicates prioritized suitability of warfighting gap solutions in oral and written formats to representatives of naval commands, engineering labs, and program offices.
Provides insight during ad hoc workshops and conferences and responds to statistical queries of systems performance.
Supervises the performance of other analysts and data engineers.

Location:
Onsite at Surface and Mine Warfighting Development Center (SMWDC)in San Diego, CA.

Masters degree in Mathematics, Statistics, Operational Research, or similar field.

Excellent analytical problem-solving skills.

Excellent communication skills.

new_jobs.title: Principal, Strategy and Operations Manager - GBSG U.S. Marketing
new_jobs.description:
Overview

Intuit is a mission-driven, global financial platform company that gives everyone the opportunity to prosper. We do this by using technology to solve our customers’ most important problems. We serve customers by finding more ways to put more money in their pockets, eliminating work and drudgery so they can focus on their lives and what matters to them, and ensuring that every financial decision that they make, they make it with confidence. We are also at an important point in Intuit’s transformation, as AI and human intelligence reshape both the experiences we deliver for customers and how we operate. Across GBSG, that means making sharper choices about where we invest, how we grow, and how we move with greater speed and focus.

As a Principal Strategy and Operations Manager, you will sit at the center of Commercial Operations, the connective tissue between strategy and execution across the commercial organization. You'll own the planning rhythm, drive the initiatives that unlock growth and profitability, and turn ambiguous business problems into decisions leadership can act on. Working at the intersection of business strategy, data analysis, and AI-enabled operations, you'll partner closely with finance, marketing, sales, and product to translate priorities into measurable outcomes and to build the operating cadence that keeps them on track. Be part of a high-growth environment where your contributions have direct, visible impact. We are looking for a strategic operator who is an avid learner, experimenter, and builder, ready to rewire how Commercial Operations runs in the AI era.

Responsibilities

Strategic Planning and Execution: Develop and execute key business initiatives to drive growth and profitability. Own and evolve the quarterly and annual planning process, helping leaders make explicit choices about priorities, investments, tradeoffs and sequencing. Use AI-assisted tools to compress cycle time and get to decisions faster.
Project Management and Cross-functional Collaboration: Manage strategic initiatives from conception to execution, collaborating with finance, marketing, sales, and product teams to ensure alignment and effective implementation. Identify and drive mitigation strategies, prioritize initiatives, and ensure alignment with cross-functional leaders to assess effectiveness and make necessary adjustments.
Performance and Data Analysis: Identify and recommend improvements to processes and systems, conducting in-depth analyses of business performance, market trends, and operational metrics to enhance efficiency and inform strategic decisions. Use AI and automation to expand the scope and speed of analysis, and to automate recurring reporting so effort shifts from data assembly to insight.
Executive Communication: Shape executive decisions by distilling complex analysis and data into clear recommendations, alternatives, and tradeoffs. Communicate those insights through crisp presentations, written narratives, and other executive-ready materials that create the clarity and alignment leaders need to make decisions and move.
AI Enablement and Velocity: Bring a demonstrated track record of using AI to meaningfully increase personal and team throughput. Design changes that address root causes rather than adding another process or layer.

Qualifications

This role demands a blend of analytical prowess, operational expertise, and leadership skills to drive effective business strategies and operational efficiencies in a complex and evolving environment.

7+ years of experience in strategy consulting, business operations, or a related field, ideally with experience in management consulting or large technology companies.
Experience leading multi-year strategy and planning, including long-range planning, annual planning, scenario development, and translating strategy into operating priorities.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with experience in data analysis, financial modeling, and KPI trend analysis. Proficiency in SQL, Python or similar for data analysis and automation scripting; experience with no‑code/low‑code platforms (e.g., Cursor, Claude Code); a plus.
Track record of working cross‑functionally with product, engineering, data scientists, and marketing channel owners. Understanding of marketing measurement, incrementality testing, and performance metrics.
Excellent verbal, written, and presentation skills. Ability to develop clear and impactful reports and presentations for stakeholders. Demonstrated leadership abilities with experience influencing and building partnerships across all levels of an organization.
Proven ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously, with strong organizational and time management skills. Comfortable working in a dynamic, high-growth environment with ambiguity.
Bachelor’s degree in Data Science, Finance, Engineering, Economics, Business, or a related field; advanced degree such as an MBA preferred.

Footer

Intuit provides a competitive compensation package with a strong pay for performance rewards approach. This position may be eligible for a cash bonus, equity rewards and benefits, in accordance with our applicable plans and programs (see more about our compensation and benefits at Intuit®: Careers | Benefits). Pay offered is based on factors such as job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and work location. To drive ongoing fair pay for employees, Intuit conducts regular comparisons across categories of ethnicity and gender.

Summary

Our Newest Opportunity:

The Retirement Solutions Operations Analyst provides day-to-day operational and analytical support to the retirement operations team. This role serves as a key liaison between branch offices, operations leadership, the M&A team, technology teams, and external partners to ensure retirement plan operations are executed accurately, efficiently, and in compliance with OneDigital Investment Advisors and Broker/Dealer standards.

The Operations Analyst plays a critical role in supporting advisors, maintaining data integrity, improving operational workflows, and enabling consistent, scalable service delivery across the retirement platform. This individual serves as a trusted subject matter resource and a proactive problem-solver — someone who takes ownership of complex workflows and projects, champions data integrity, and drives continuous improvement, including through the thoughtful use of AI and automation.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities (includes but is not limited to):

Operational Support & Advisor Enablement

Serve as a primary point of contact for field offices and internal stakeholders on retirement operations-related inquiries, ensuring issues are resolved with accuracy, professionalism, and urgency.
Assist with managing the Retirement Solutions Operations (RPS OPS) shared email inbox, maintaining timely and professional responsiveness to advisors and colleagues across the organization.
Act as a subject matter resource for RPS OPS processes, applying industry knowledge and sound judgment to resolve operational issues and escalate to leadership when appropriate.
Support operational lifecycle events including cost center changes, plan terminations, and related administrative actions.
Maintain strong working relationships with Accounting and Finance partners to support training, issue resolution, and operational alignment.
Lead and manage operations projects from initiation to completion, keeping all tasks on target, on time, and aligned with team priorities.
Analyze reports indicating discrepancies in plan counts, advisors, or recordkeepers, and act to resolve identified issues.
Identify opportunities to improve operational workflows and contribute to the development of scalable processes — including the use of AI — that elevate service delivery across the retirement platform.
Support supervision and training of interns or Operations Associates on account setup and documentation review processes.

M&A Onboarding & Transition Management

Work closely with the Retirement Solutions Operations Manager to execute retirement operations responsibilities tied to new business from acquired firms or individual advisors transferring blocks of business.
Participate in weekly M&A team meetings as needed, representing retirement operations and contributing to transaction readiness and transition planning.
Serve as a knowledgeable resource on best practices, policies, and procedures throughout the transition process, ensuring a smooth and compliant handoff.
Review data and coordinate with incoming firms on current platforms and operational requirements.
Develop productive advisor and firm relationships over a compressed timeframe to facilitate efficient and effective transitions.
Manage the preparation and processing of all transition paperwork, serving as an operations contact for incoming firms on paperwork-related matters.
Liaise with Accounting to ensure all Retirement Plans are tracked through to first payment, maintaining accurate records and proactive follow-up throughout.

Qualifications, Skills And Requirements

Conformity with all legal and regulatory requirements and guidelines associated with FINRA, SEC, and OneDigital Investment Advisors LLC compliance standards is required.
Demonstrated understanding of investment accounts, registrations, and compliance within RIA and Broker/Dealer environments.
Proficiency in Salesforce and the full Microsoft 365 Suite (Outlook, Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Teams) is required.
Experience with Fi360, Smartsheet, Orion, or other finance- or retirement-related vendor platforms is preferred.
Comfort working with data — including the ability to identify discrepancies, maintain data integrity, and produce clear operational reporting.
Comfort using AI to automate manual processes, create effective templates, and improve written communication.
Strong consultative, critical-thinking, and problem-solving skills with a bias toward action and resolution.
Exceptional organizational skills with the demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities, meet deadlines, and hold self and others accountable for deliverables.
Strong project management capabilities; able to drive complex, multi-stakeholder initiatives from planning through execution.
Outstanding written and verbal communication skills; able to present clearly and succinctly across diverse audiences and adapt communication style accordingly.
High degree of composure and adaptability — able to manage increasing workloads in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment with professionalism and calm.
Customer-focused mindset with interpersonal agility to work effectively across different personality types and organizational levels.
Superior follow-through and follow-up discipline; thrives in a high-energy, collaborative team environment.
Previous experience in a customer or client support role is preferred.

Education, Training And Experience

An undergraduate degree in Business, Information Technology, Accounting, Finance, Economics, or a related field is required; equivalent work experience will be considered.
4–5 years of business experience required, preferably in management of technology, processes, and people within the investment or financial services industry.
Required: Proficiency in Salesforce and the Microsoft 365 Suite.
Preferred: Experience with Fi360, Smartsheet, Orion, or other finance- or retirement-related vendor platforms.

Role Overview

We are seeking a visionary and technical Senior Program Manager who is also a business domain expert in HRIT. This role will lead an enterprise-wide migration, implementation, and long-term support of Oracle Fusion HCM Cloud applications. You will bridge the gap between executive strategy and hands-on execution, owning the end-to-end strategic roadmap, governance, and deployment while leading technical design and issue resolution.

Key Responsibilities

Define the enterprise migration strategy, delivery methodology, Redwood UI rollout plans, and deployment roadmaps.
Establish program steering committees, corporate risk management frameworks, and KPIs to track migration and platform health.
Act as the primary liaison between HR executive leadership, IT executives, and external implementation partners to map business processes.
Own fiscal responsibility for the program budget, ensuring cost controls and resource optimization.
Proactively identify, track, and manage program risks, including business continuity disruption, data loss, and deployment friction.
Formulate robust rollback strategies, disaster recovery plans, and operational workarounds to protect core HR operations.
Collaborate with business stakeholders to translate functional requirements into technical design documents.
Oversee complex data migration strategies, data cleansing protocols, and historical data archiving.
Diagnose, replicate, and resolve complex functional and technical issues for critical service requests.
Guide technical teams on complex integrations and configurations between Oracle Cloud HCM and third-party systems using Oracle Integration Cloud (OIC) and Fast Formulas.
Ensure the migrated platform adheres to data privacy laws, data security frameworks, and unit testing parameters.
Matrix-manage a team of 30+ internal functional analysts, technical developers, and change management specialists.
Drive accountability for System Integrators (SIs) and external consultants, monitoring SLA adherence and solution quality.

Required Qualifications

Experience:
12+ years of progressive techno-functional IT/HRIS program management experience, with at least 6 years of direct experience with Oracle HCM Cloud products/solutions. This must include a proven track record leading at least two full-lifecycle, large-scale migrations for organizations with 10,000+ employees. A minimum of 5 years in a Program Manager role managing multi-stream programs is required.

Technical Skills:
Expert functional and technical implementation/support knowledge across key Fusion modules, including Payroll, Core HR, Compensation, Benefits, Time & Labor, Talent, and Absence Management. Strong understanding of Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI), HDL (HCM Data Loader), Fast Formulas, and Oracle Integration Cloud (OIC). Practical experience or exposure handling Redwood UI rollouts and enhancements is necessary. Mastery of Oracle Unified Method (OUM), Agile, and traditional Waterfall project management methodologies is also required.

Education:
Bachelor’s degree in computer science, Management Information Systems (MIS), Human Resources, or a related field.

Certifications:

Oracle Cloud HCM Certified Implementation Specialist
PMP (Project Management Professional)

Preferred Qualifications

Prosci Certified Change Management Professional
HRIP (Human Resources Information Professional) from IHRIM
Snowflake experience is a plus.

new_jobs.title: Sales Enablement Program Manager
new_jobs.description:
Description

Join Team CARFAX as a Sales Enablement Program Manager

Isn't it time you bragged about where you work? At CARFAX, we do, every day. We pride ourselves on being mission-focused on helping to grow a brand built on accuracy and integrity. We care deeply about our products and our customers. We’re more than just a company: We help millions of consumers make more-informed decisions every day. We know that our teammates are our most valuable asset, and we value a balanced life while tackling challenging projects in a fast-paced environment.

About The Role

CARFAX is investing in its Revenue Enablement function, and the Sales Enablement Program Manager is central to that effort. This is a hands-on, high-impact role focused on sharpening the skills, process discipline, and execution of our DBU sales teams — Field Sales, Hybrid Field Sales, Strategic Sales, and Inside Sales.

You’ll spend the majority of your time embedded in the flow of the sales org: coaching reps and frontline managers, reinforcing our sales process and methodology, and building the programs, content, and tools that help sellers win. You’ll also serve as a strategic partner to sales leadership — bringing field insight and enablement expertise into decisions about process, change, and go-to-market execution. This is a builder’s role on a growing team, so you’ll help shape how enablement operates at CARFAX while delivering results from day one.

What You’ll Be Doing

Enable all DBU sales roles. Serve as the dedicated enablement partner to Field Sales, Strategic Sales, and Inside Sales — tailoring programs, coaching, and content to the distinct motions, customer profiles, and performance goals of each team. One size doesn’t fit all; what works for a field rep calling on independent dealers is different from what an inside seller needs to convert on the phone.
Build and lead training and coaching. Own the design, delivery, and continuous improvement of sales training on core selling fundamentals — discovery, value articulation, objection handling, negotiation, and pipeline management. Provide hands-on coaching to reps and managers through field ride-alongs, call reviews, and deal reviews. Equip frontline managers to reinforce these skills with their own teams so your impact scales across the org. Best-in-class enablement functions treat training as a continuous discipline, not a one-time event — this mindset is the foundation of the role.
Reinforce process, methodology, and tools. Drive consistent adoption of CARFAX’s sales process and methodology through sustained, ongoing reinforcement. Champion adoption of the supporting tech stack — CRM, conversation intelligence, enablement platforms — so reps work smarter and sales leaders have the visibility they need to coach effectively.
Build assets and codify best practices. Create and maintain polished, field-ready sales assets — playbooks, battle cards, talk tracks, pitch decks, and process guides. Surface what top performers do differently through field observation, call reviews, and win/loss patterns, and systematically distribute those insights across the sales org. Ensuring reps have access to the right content at the right moment in the sales cycle is a core enablement discipline.
Partner on the onboarding handoff. Work closely with the Onboarding Lead to ensure a seamless transition from new hire onboarding into ongoing, role-based enablement. This role does not own onboarding, but its success depends on a tight partnership with the person who does.
Serve as a strategic partner to sales leadership. Act as a trusted advisor to DBU sales leadership on how to raise seller performance and execution quality. Bring the field’s perspective into internal decisions on process roll-outs, change management, and product launches — ensuring the field is ready to execute before go-to-market, not after.
Collaborate cross-functionally. Partner with Revenue Operations to define and track the KPIs that demonstrate enablement’s impact on pipeline health, conversion rates, and revenue performance. Partner with Marketing on sales assets, messaging, and go-to-market motions — so programs are data-informed and what reps carry into the field is aligned, current, and on-brand.

Required

What we’re looking for:

3+ years of sales enablement experience, ideally supporting multiple, distinct sales motions simultaneously.
Experience carrying a sales quota — you’ve sold, and you understand the seller’s world firsthand.
A demonstrated track record of designing and delivering training and coaching programs that measurably change rep behavior and drive revenue outcomes.
Strong facilitation, communication, and coaching skills — both in-person and virtually — including the ability to create compelling, polished presentations in PowerPoint (or equivalent tools).
The ability to build trust and influence without authority across reps, managers, senior leadership, and cross-functional partners.
Comfort operating in a build-from-scratch environment where structure, programs, and processes don’t fully exist yet — and you’ll help create them.
Experience with a formal sales methodology (e.g., MEDDIC/MEDDPICC, Integrity Selling, Challenger, SPIN, or similar) and a track record of reinforcing it in the field over time.
Ability to travel up to 10% of the time to coach reps in the field and support team events.

Preferred

Automotive industry or automotive technology experience — familiarity with how dealerships operate, how they buy, and what they value is a meaningful advantage in this role.
Experience supporting a blend of field, strategic/enterprise, and inside sales teams within a single organization.
Hands-on experience with conversation intelligence tools (e.g., Gong, Chorus), Salesforce, learning management systems (LMS), and content management systems (CMS).

What’s In It For You

Competitive compensation, benefits and generous time-off policies
4-Day summer work weeks and a winter holiday break
401(k) / DCPP matching
Annual bonus program
Casual, dog-friendly, and innovative office spaces.

Don’t Just Take Our Word For It

13x VA Best Places to Work
12x Top Workplaces in Washington (Presented by The Washington Post and WTOP)
9x Washingtonian Great Place to Work
5x USA Today Top Workplaces
5x St. Louis Post-Dispatch Best Places to Work

The anticipated annual base salary range for this position is $110,000 - $150,000. Actual compensation within this range will be determined based on a variety of factors, including geographic location, relevant experience, skills, qualifications, and internal equity considerations.

Carfax is committed to providing competitive compensation that reflects local market conditions and individual contributions. In addition to base salary, employees may be eligible for incentive compensation, long-term incentives, and a comprehensive benefits package, where applicable.

About CARFAX And S&P Global Mobility

S&P Global has recently announced the intent to separate our Mobility Segment into a standalone public company.

CARFAX, part of S&P Global Mobility, helps millions of people every day confidently shop, buy, service and sell used cars with innovative solutions powered by CARFAX vehicle history information. The expert in vehicle history since 1984, CARFAX provides exclusive services like CARFAX Used Car Listings, CARFAX Car Care, CARFAX History-Based Value and the flagship CARFAX® Vehicle History Report™ to consumers and the automotive industry.
